sentences.text: An amber weather warning has come into force in parts of the UK as Storm Austen brings a swathe of powerful winds and heavy rain on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Amber warning in place as Storm Austen hits parts of UK

sentences.text: South West England is forecast to be worst hit by the storm which the Met Office warns could bring travel disruption, power cuts and a possible danger to life.
sentences.article_title: Amber warning in place as Storm Austen hits parts of UK

sentences.text: Wind gusts of 60-70mph, with 80mph in exposed locations, are forecast across Cornwall and parts of Devon, where the Met Office warning is in force until 10:00 BST.

sentences.text: Wind gust of 45-60mph are forecast more widely across most of England and Wales, where two less severe yellow warnings will be in force throughout Friday.

sentences.text: A strong jet stream is needed to rapidly develop powerful wind storms.
sentences.article_title: Amber warning in place as Storm Austen hits parts of UK

sentences.text: The process involved in creating such storms involves shifting warmer air northwards and cooler air southwards across vast areas of the Atlantic.

sentences.text: These temperature contrasts can provide a fertile environment for new low pressure systems to develop and if these subsequently get steered beneath a developmental area of a powerful jet stream, they can rapidly develop to create a new named storm with damaging winds.

sentences.text: Six days is a long time in The Celebrity Traitors.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity Traitors - paranoia deepens as traitor behaviour splits opinion

sentences.text: So it was a relief to be put out of our misery as last Friday's literal yawn-fest came to its slow-burning conclusion; the traitorous trio eventually succeeding in their mission to kill in plain sight.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity Traitors - paranoia deepens as traitor behaviour splits opinion

sentences.text: The snoozefest - which involved reluctant traitor James Acaster making faithful Ross Kemp yawn by boring him to tears - meant the paranoid EastEnders star was finally put out of his misery.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity Traitors - paranoia deepens as traitor behaviour splits opinion

sentences.text: On learning his fate, the actor turned to Shakespeare - who else?
sentences.article_title: Celebrity Traitors - paranoia deepens as traitor behaviour splits opinion

sentences.text: "To thine own self be true," he declared, quoting Polonius from Hamlet.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity Traitors - paranoia deepens as traitor behaviour splits opinion

sentences.text: As usual at breakfast, the faithfuls seated early mused over who may have been murdered overnight: "If Jerry's not here, I don't think I can handle it," Romesh Ranganathan confessed.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity Traitors - paranoia deepens as traitor behaviour splits opinion

sentences.text: Jerry Hall was charmingly late to the party.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity Traitors - paranoia deepens as traitor behaviour splits opinion

sentences.text: After everyone had discussed Ross's demise, she piped up in her famous Texan drawl: "Is Ross gone?" As the typical off-the-wall theories began to swirl, Jerry later told Miranda Hart she suspected fellow faithful James Blunt - for the very plausible reason that "his face is redder than a fox's ass at gooseberry time".
sentences.article_title: Celebrity Traitors - paranoia deepens as traitor behaviour splits opinion

sentences.text: It's as good a reason as any proffered so far this series.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity Traitors - paranoia deepens as traitor behaviour splits opinion

sentences.text: Miranda felt there were more complex olfactory notes at play: "A mix of salmon, cheap cologne and crotch." Delightful.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity Traitors - paranoia deepens as traitor behaviour splits opinion

sentences.text: The mission involved each player having to build a shield on a plinth in front of them out of 3D jigsaw-type pieces which were buried in troughs in sawdust.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity Traitors - paranoia deepens as traitor behaviour splits opinion

sentences.text: Think Krypton Factor meets lucky dip.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity Traitors - paranoia deepens as traitor behaviour splits opinion

sentences.text: At three intervals, a bell would ring, and the players all had to stop and put on blindfolds for a few minutes.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity Traitors - paranoia deepens as traitor behaviour splits opinion

sentences.text: The traitors could then remove theirs and go about sabotaging the handiwork of anyone they fancied.
sentences.article_title: Celebrity Traitors - paranoia deepens as traitor behaviour splits opinion

sentences.text: And while James A revealed he was "starting to have more fun" after murdering poor Ross, if there was a prize for the worst traitor of all time, he would still smash it.

sentences.text: He was too scared to take off his blindfold and remove any shield pieces from the faithfuls, leaving the dirty work - and all the risk - to fellow traitors Maya Jama and King Kenny.

sentences.text: Douglas Craigie, Murdo Morrison and Norman Murray had been fishing off the north coast of Lewis Items belonging to a fishing boat that vanished off the north coast of the Isle of Lewis last week have been recovered as the search for the vessel and two missing crew members continues.

sentences.text: Norman "Tam" Murray, 40 and Murdo Morrison, 23, were on board the Kilda when it disappeared on 13 October.
sentences.article_title: Items recovered in search for missing fishing boat and crew

sentences.text: The body of crewmate Douglas Craigie, 49, was recovered from the sea in the early hours of the following morning by rescuers.
sentences.article_title: Items recovered in search for missing fishing boat and crew

sentences.text: On Thursday, police confirmed that items belonging to the vessel had been recovered from what was described as "an area of interest" off the coast near Port of Ness.

sentences.article_title: Items recovered in search for missing fishing boat and crew

sentences.text: Defence Secretary Wes Streeting has made headlines in today's papers after launching a national campaign on public preparedness for disruption caused by natural disasters and cyber attacks.
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Prepare for the worst' and 'Covid report fallout'

sentences.text: The Daily Telegraph reports on Britons being asked to make "Be ready" kits for emergencies, "including three days' worth of non-perishable food and bottled water, an FM radio and blankets".
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Prepare for the worst' and 'Covid report fallout'

sentences.text: Meanwhile, the Metro warns readers to "prepare for the worst" after websites around the world were taken offline after cyber-security flaws were revealed in a globally-used programming language, PHP.
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Prepare for the worst' and 'Covid report fallout'

sentences.text: "In the UK, 32 government services were down", the paper reports, before asking the question "are you emergency ready?" The Independent leads on Streeting's messaging for Britons to be prepared in case "'state-sponsored terrorism' disrupts everyday life".
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Prepare for the worst' and 'Covid report fallout'

sentences.text: The government's campaign comes as global security flaw knocked dozens of government services offline, the paper says.
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Prepare for the worst' and 'Covid report fallout'

sentences.text: Similarly, the Guardian leads on UK households being urged to stockpile enough food and water to "survive 72 hours in a crisis", the Guardian reports.
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Prepare for the worst' and 'Covid report fallout'

sentences.text: The new guidance from the government follows concerns on "climate change, technological dependency and hostile state threats", the paper says.
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Prepare for the worst' and 'Covid report fallout'

sentences.text: Streeting "issues checklist for coping after catastrophe" and to "be prepared with 3 days of supplies", the Times reports.
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Prepare for the worst' and 'Covid report fallout'

sentences.text: Elsewhere British singer Raye is pictured singing on stage as a "golden wonder" following her Mercury Prize win.
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Prepare for the worst' and 'Covid report fallout'

sentences.text: "Don't Panic!" the Daily Mail instructs after ministers were "accused of lecturing families" to stockpile "in case of a national emergency".
sentences.article_title: The Papers: 'Prepare for the worst' and 'Covid report fallout'

sentences.text: Elsewhere on the page, Catherine, Princess of Wales, is pictured with her son Prince George, who she is said to be missing while he is at Eton.

sentences.text: Former Health Secretary Matt Hancock has been heavily criticised after another Covid inquiry over "untested patients being discharged into care homes where tens of thousands of residents died", the Daily Mirror reports.

sentences.text: "Bereaved families are calling for Hancock to be stripped of his Right Honourable title" following his handling of Covid, the paper says.

sentences.text: Private companies buying up care homes for older people in England could undermine the government's ambition to create a universal care service , the regulator says.
sentences.article_title: Private care home investors a risk to public sector, regulator says

sentences.text: The Care Quality Commission's annual report , external highlights how an increasing share of the care home market is owned by large firms - the five biggest have increased their share of the market by 26% in the last two years, driven by interest from US property investors.
sentences.article_title: Private care home investors a risk to public sector, regulator says

sentences.text: Between them they own around one in seven homes.
sentences.article_title: Private care home investors a risk to public sector, regulator says

sentences.text: While there could be benefits, there are concerns the trend can lead to higher prices and a reduction in the quality of care - something the CQC says needs to be monitored.
sentences.article_title: Private care home investors a risk to public sector, regulator says

sentences.text: Meanwhile, home care, providing support to help people wash and dress in their own home, has become more fragmented, with a greater number of smaller providers.
sentences.article_title: Private care home investors a risk to public sector, regulator says

sentences.text: The CQC says this could create inefficiencies - nearly a third of these services are providing care to four or fewer people.
sentences.article_title: Private care home investors a risk to public sector, regulator says

sentences.text: In contrast, there are few smaller care homes judged important for providing specialist and personalised care.
sentences.article_title: Private care home investors a risk to public sector, regulator says

sentences.text: Small care homes have always represented a tiny proportion of the care home market, but over the last 14 years the numbers have fallen significantly, particularly those that combine care with nursing support, which are down by a quarter.
sentences.article_title: Private care home investors a risk to public sector, regulator says

sentences.text: The CQC says the funding system remains fragile – people using care services either self-fund or, for the poorest, the state helps to pay for their costs.
sentences.article_title: Private care home investors a risk to public sector, regulator says

sentences.text: And in some areas, providers are increasingly turning to self-funders, making it more difficult for councils to buy the care they need for those relying on state help.
sentences.article_title: Private care home investors a risk to public sector, regulator says

sentences.text: CQC chief inspector of adult social care, Chris Badger, said the reshaping of the market was happening "largely by accident rather than design", driven by a combination of economic pressure and the problems some councils were having in buying services for those relying on state-funded care.
sentences.article_title: Private care home investors a risk to public sector, regulator says

sentences.text: He said this government's renewed focus on social care – Andy Burnham made it one of his key priorities when he became prime minister – was welcome.
sentences.article_title: Private care home investors a risk to public sector, regulator says

sentences.text: But he said it was important the market was "shaped around what's best for people".
sentences.article_title: Private care home investors a risk to public sector, regulator says

sentences.text: "A clearer vision is needed," he added.
sentences.article_title: Private care home investors a risk to public sector, regulator says

sentences.text: Hugh Alderwick, of the Health Foundation think-tank, said the report by the CQC "lays bare the massive challenges" facing the government.
sentences.article_title: Private care home investors a risk to public sector, regulator says

sentences.text: "The prime minister's commitment to reforming the sector provides an opportunity to fundamentally redraw the state's offer on social care.
sentences.article_title: Private care home investors a risk to public sector, regulator says

sentences.text: "But change is needed now to strengthen the fundamentals of the system.
sentences.article_title: Private care home investors a risk to public sector, regulator says

sentences.text: "Unless we get some real progress in a funding settlement, the trend of smaller homes closing will be a trend that will continue." The Department of Health and Social Care said the report demonstrated the "scale of the challenge this government inherited", but said it was committed to overhauling social care.
sentences.article_title: Private care home investors a risk to public sector, regulator says

sentences.text: Nottinghamshire Police said the officer approached two people in Angel Row before being shot in the foot A 27-year-old woman has been charged after a police officer was shot in Nottingham city centre.
sentences.article_title: Woman charged after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: Nottinghamshire Police said the officer was shot in the foot after he approached a man and a woman at a bus stop in Angel Row shortly before 04:50 BST on Sunday.
sentences.article_title: Woman charged after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: The male officer remains in hospital receiving treatment, the force added.
sentences.article_title: Woman charged after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: Aisha Zaman, of Collison Street, Hyson Green, has been charged with possession of a prohibited firearm and possession of that firearm with intent to commit an indictable offence.
sentences.article_title: Woman charged after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: Police said the charge came after "consultation with the Crown Prosecution Service".
sentences.article_title: Woman charged after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: Zaman has been remanded into custody and will appear before Nottingham Magistrates' Court on Friday, police added.
sentences.article_title: Woman charged after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: Several other people have been arrested in connection with the incident, including two men, 24 and 30, and two women, 25 and 21, who have been arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender.
sentences.article_title: Woman charged after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: A 35-year-old man and a 33-year-old woman have also been arrested on suspicion of possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life and assisting an offender.
sentences.article_title: Woman charged after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: Both remain in police custody.
sentences.article_title: Woman charged after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: Det Ch Supt Rich Bull, who is leading the investigation, said the "outpouring of support" for the officer had been "greatly appreciated".
sentences.article_title: Woman charged after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: "We continue to support him as he undergoes further treatment in hospital and keeping him and his family fully informed of the developments in this investigation." sentences.text: RAF A400M planes will be able to fight wildfires if fire crews request them Military planes and helicopters will be drafted in to tackle wildfires, Prime Minister Andy Burnham is to tell the UK's first summit on the issue.
sentences.article_title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: Civilian fire services in all four nations will be able to request the support of the Royal Air Force's Chinook helicopters and A400M planes to fight wildfires on tough terrain such as remote moorland and steep hillsides.
sentences.article_title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: Burnham said the measures were needed because "we cannot put people through another summer like this one".
sentences.article_title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: The government will host its first "wildfire resilience summit" on Friday to discuss how to prevent, respond to and recover from such blazes after a record-breaking summer 2026.
sentences.article_title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: There have been 1,350 wildfires in England and Wales this year, an all-time high and up by more than 300 on last year and more than 1,000 on 2024, according to figures from the National Fire Chiefs Council .
sentences.article_title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: Records for the number of reported wildfires were also broken in 2022 and 2025 - but the UK's Climate Change Committee has warned the risk will rise in the coming decades.
sentences.article_title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said this was the first time the RAF's Chinooks and the four-engine A400Ms were being equipped to tackle wildfires.
sentences.article_title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: Some areas struggled with no air assistance in the summer.
sentences.article_title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: Chinooks have practised picking up and dropping water from firefighting buckets in Portland harbour, UK RAF Chinook crews have already helped respond , external to wildfires in Cyprus.
sentences.article_title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: In addition to military aircraft, the government said it would also spend £45m on wildfire-specific personal protective equipment for firefighters on the ground.
sentences.article_title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: It is lighter than current firefighting equipment which is designed for fires in buildings and not meant to be worn for a long time, the government added.
sentences.article_title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: Ministers are also pledging a £25m scheme from April 2027 to April 2029 to restore dried-out peatlands in England so they are natural firebreaks, and financial support for farmers to fireproof their land such as by digging ponds.
sentences.article_title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: "The government will also look at tougher local restrictions or product bans to stop people starting fires when the risk is high," a briefing ahead of the summit said, following a temporary ban on disposable BBQs .
sentences.article_title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: Burnham will meet fire chiefs, local leaders and experts from tech companies at the summit.
sentences.article_title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: "I stood in Stourbridge and watched families lose everything," he said on Thursday, recounting the night of a wildfire that destroyed 19 homes in the West Midlands in August.
sentences.article_title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: Firefighters tackled wildfires across the UK over the summer, including here in Ebbw Vale, Wales MPs said the current system for obtaining aerial firefighting support was "no longer fit for purpose".
sentences.article_title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: At the summit, a "Wildfires AI Unit" will be announced to combine universities, tech firms and officials on the Cobra emergency committee, along with Met Office wildfire forecasts and closer work with devolved governments.
sentences.article_title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: In August, the government convened a Cobra meeting before sending an emergency alert to millions of phones across England and Wales - which sparked a backlash from some .
sentences.article_title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: Summer 2026 was the UK's hottest on record, according to the Met Office.
sentences.article_title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: In a study on how this summer was impacted by human-induced climate change, it said the heat experienced was made 130 times more likely .
sentences.article_title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.article_title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: "Nature is our greatest ally in preventing wildfires starting in the first place," she added.
sentences.article_title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says

sentences.text: Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg Meta has agreed to a new deal with chief executive Mark Zuckerberg to prevent him from leaving California over a proposed state tax on billionaires.

sentences.text: Tommy Robinson, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, has been giving evidence at Southwark Crown Court Political activist Tommy Robinson has told a court he hired private detectives to track down and photograph two reporters to "put pressure" on them.
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: The 43-year-old from Bedfordshire, real name Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, told Southwark Crown Court he was "shocked and scared" when the Daily Mail published a story accusing him of "stoking race riots from his sunbed".
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: He has denied two charges of harassment causing fear of violence to reporters Andrew Young and Jacob Dirnhuber after the 2024 Southport attacks.
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: Robinson is accused of writing posts on X, sending direct messages and making phone calls that made the two journalists fear the risk of vigilante attacks .
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: He denied wanting to expose the journalists to threats of violence, and said he felt his actions were "totally reasonable... under the circumstances".
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: Robinson wiped tears from his eyes as he gave evidence in the dock about events in August 2024 In early August 2024, he was on holiday at the Atlantica Mare resort in Cyprus, as riots took place in England following the murders of three girls in Southport.
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: Robinson was on holiday with "my ex-wife, my three children and three other families and their children", he told the jury.
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: He said he had managed to keep her and children out of sight "for 17 years -and that meant travelling in separate cars".
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: In the witness stand, he claimed he had not "stoked" the riots, but tried to "calm" things.
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: When the Daily Mail published an article online, he said he was "shocked".
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: "I'm scared because the Mail Online is the biggest publication in the world." He said the original article allowed people to quickly work out where he was holidaying, and included an image of his wife.
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: He panicked, thinking it would "change her life forever", he said.
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: Robinson struggled to answer a question about how his children were affected by the story, as he took tissues and wiped tears from his eyes.
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: He replied that he left the hotel after the story was published, and that his family moved to a different location within the hotel following advice from security.
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: Robinson told the jury his 12-year-old daughter had received rape threats, and his ex-wife had previously been threatened with an acid attack.
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: He said he tried to call the editor-in-chief of the Daily Mail, but he would not answer.
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: "They could have run the story without giving my location," he said.
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: "They shouldn't have done that and this is not journalism, this is endangering us." Tommy Robinson denies the charges of harassment causing fear of violence against two Daily Mail journalists The court heard how Robinson used private investigators to obtain telephone numbers and emails for the journalists.
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: He phoned Andrew Young, the Daily Mail reporter who had tracked him down in Cyprus.
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: "I wanted my ex-wife's picture removed from the publication," he said.
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: "I said: 'You're not going to get away from this problem...You've endangered my children'." He told jurors he wanted to "find the journalists" and ask them "on camera" to explain how he was "stoking race riots".
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: Robinson said he had asked the private investigators to try to get pictures of the journalists and their family members.
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: Young said he had to use private security after the defendant posted pictures on X of his wife and daughter near their home, with their faces cropped off.
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: And Dirnhuber said in a statement read to the jury that he left his home for a week after Robinson published a picture of him outside his house on X.
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: He said he was trying to "bring the Daily Mail to the table" and did not know the reporters were "in fear".
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: "That wasn't my intention at all," he said.
sentences.article_title: Tommy Robinson hired detectives to find journalists, court told

sentences.text: Melvin West has been sentenced to three years in jail A man who used a Stanley knife to cut a rare 17th Century world map out of an atlas at a museum library has been jailed for three years.
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: Melvin West, 70, sliced the map from a 1684 atlas by Dutch cartographer Frederik de Wit while viewing it at the Caird Library, part of the National Maritime Museum in Greenwich, in February 2025.
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: The map has never been found, and a judge at Woolwich Crown Court said West had led the court, police and museum a "merry dance" over where it was.
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: The Metropolitan Police has appealed for anyone who knows where it is to come forward.
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: This video can not be played Man sentenced for stealing antique map from museum in Greenwich The double hemisphere world map, known as Nova Orbis Tabula, was one of 12 in the atlas, and is studied by scholars around the world.
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: The court heard West, from Chingford in east London, had viewed the atlas on 19 and 20 December 2024 and again on the day before the theft.
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: Staff called police after finding a knife on the floor of the viewing room where he had been looking at the atlas.
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: They then discovered the map had been cut out.
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: West was arrested at his home in March 2025, but the map was not there.
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: He pleaded guilty at Bromley Magistrates' Court in May to theft, criminal damage and possession of a bladed article.
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: Prosecution barrister Damian Warburton said the complete atlas had been worth about £50,000 and the map alone could fetch £6,000 on the black market.
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: The atlas is now valued at £20,000, but he told the court the "cultural loss far outweighs the financial loss".
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: The stolen map, like the one pictured, was a double hemisphere Defence barrister Jessica Flain said West had partly paid a man to restore the map, but he would not hand it back until the full fee was settled.
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: She asked for sentencing to be adjourned for seven days so a friend could pay the balance and West could take the map to Charing Cross Police Station.
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: Judge Charlotte Welsh refused, saying she did "not believe a word of it".
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: She said West had told the court in June that he could return the map within seven days, and in August that it was with a friend and he would retrieve it once he had recovered from heart surgery.
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: "Again, that appears to have been a lie," she said.
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: "You were charged in February.
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: You have had eight months to return the map." The judge said she believed West had a buyer in mind and had stolen the map "to order".
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: The court heard he had 27 convictions for 107 offences in the UK and abroad, mostly for dishonesty and including 41 thefts.
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: They included a burglary conviction in Hungary in 2011 and a theft conviction in France in 2013, and he had also been convicted under various identities.
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: Flain said West, a father of two, was "ashamed and embarrassed" and had been in debt and unable to meet basic living costs.
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: She described the offence as "a short-term, pressured decision by an elderly man living in difficult circumstances".
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: Judge Welsh said the map was of "international cultural significance" and the damage had "permanently diminished what can be learned from it".
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: The court was told the two digital copies of the atlas are incomplete.
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: West was jailed for three years for criminal damage, with concurrent sentences of 16 months for theft and six months for possessing a bladed article.
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: The judge refused to suspend the sentence, saying immediate custody was needed "to deter other people from doing precisely what you have".
sentences.article_title: Map thief leads 'merry dance' with return promises

sentences.text: Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch speaking at the Police Federation conference in London Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has criticised punishments for people who intervene to "do the right thing" in a speech at the Police Federation conference.
sentences.article_title: Police should not be scared to wade in to stop wrongdoing, says Badenoch

sentences.text: Telling delegates she was "not scared to wade in", she called for more support for members of the public as well as police officers who step in to stop wrongdoing.

sentences.article_title: Police should not be scared to wade in to stop wrongdoing, says Badenoch

sentences.text: "Whether it's hounding brave and elderly veterans through the courts, hounding police officers who try to do the right thing, or even ordinary members of the public who step in to help only to find that they're in trouble themselves.
sentences.article_title: Police should not be scared to wade in to stop wrongdoing, says Badenoch

sentences.article_title: Police should not be scared to wade in to stop wrongdoing, says Badenoch

The Conservative leader listed police officers who have been killed in the line of duty, such as PCs Matthew Blades and Tom Clough who died in the Cleveland A66 crash, and PC Andrew Harper , killed investigating a quad bike theft.
sentences.article_title: Police should not be scared to wade in to stop wrongdoing, says Badenoch

sentences.text: She also attacked police being  investigated following controversial cases, including the case of 24-year-old Chris Kaba , who was shot by Sgt Matthew Blake in 2022 after he tried to ram his way past police cars.
sentences.article_title: Police should not be scared to wade in to stop wrongdoing, says Badenoch

sentences.text: The police officer was put on trial for murder before being cleared, with Badenoch saying his "job was made harder because he didn't get the backing he deserved".

sentences.text: Badenoch also attacked Labour, saying: "I think it is telling that for two years in a row, the Labour Government has not sent anyone to address this conference – not the policing minister, not the Home Secretary.

sentences.text: "You are the ones who enforce the law.

sentences.article_title: Police should not be scared to wade in to stop wrongdoing, says Badenoch

sentences.text: The UK has accused the Yantar, operated by Russia's Ministry of Defence, of mapping underwater infrastructure The government has outlined new measures to protect the UK's undersea internet cables amid increased fears of Russian interference.
sentences.article_title: UK plans emergency powers to protect undersea cables

sentences.text: Ministers are set to gain powers to order telecom companies to remove or disable services during national security emergencies, as well as granting officials access to sites including cable landing stations.
sentences.article_title: UK plans emergency powers to protect undersea cables

sentences.text: The government has also outlined plans for stronger criminal penalties for those convicted of tampering with either undersea internet cables or energy pipelines.
sentences.article_title: UK plans emergency powers to protect undersea cables

sentences.text: The new powers would be backed up with prison sentences of up to 14 years for intentional conduct, 10 years for reckless conduct and two years for grossly negligent conduct, alongside unlimited fines.
sentences.article_title: UK plans emergency powers to protect undersea cables

sentences.text: It comes amid growing fears of suspicious activity in UK waters, and concerns that legal powers over the network have not kept pace with its growing importance to national security.
sentences.article_title: UK plans emergency powers to protect undersea cables

sentences.text: An extensive network of undersea cables and pipelines owned and operated primarily by the private sector are thought to carry almost all the UK's international data traffic and three-quarters of its gas supplies.
sentences.article_title: UK plans emergency powers to protect undersea cables

sentences.text: The growing importance of undersea infrastructure prompted a parliamentary report last year , external to warn of security vulnerabilities in areas including transport and supply chains, financial services and payment systems.
sentences.article_title: UK plans emergency powers to protect undersea cables

sentences.text: The UK and its Nato allies are concerned about the risk Russia poses to offshore infrastructure.
sentences.article_title: UK plans emergency powers to protect undersea cables

sentences.text: In April, the government accused Russian submarines of conducting a covert operation over cables and pipelines in waters north of the UK.
sentences.article_title: UK plans emergency powers to protect undersea cables

sentences.text: The UK has also accused Russia of mapping undersea infrastructure using spy ships.
sentences.article_title: UK plans emergency powers to protect undersea cables

sentences.text: Last year, it revealed the Royal Navy had tracked one such suspected ship, the Yantar, after it passed near UK waters.
sentences.article_title: UK plans emergency powers to protect undersea cables

sentences.text: Russia has denied the claims, and accused the UK of stirring up tensions through "anti-Russian alarmism".
sentences.article_title: UK plans emergency powers to protect undersea cables

sentences.text: In a policy paper on Thursday, the government said it currently lacked emergency powers to deal with incidents affecting undersea infrastructure.
sentences.article_title: UK plans emergency powers to protect undersea cables

sentences.text: It added there were currently no equivalent powers to measures that allow intervention in the water and air traffic sectors, whilst broader powers for national emergencies could prove too slow to exercise during a crisis.
sentences.article_title: UK plans emergency powers to protect undersea cables

sentences.text: It is now proposing new powers that would allow it to force telecoms companies to hand over information or modify or disable services in connection with specific threats or incidents.
sentences.article_title: UK plans emergency powers to protect undersea cables

sentences.text: The changes will require new legislation, to be set out after a consultation with industry closing in January.
sentences.article_title: UK plans emergency powers to protect undersea cables

sentences.text: Companies that refused to comply with the orders could be fined up to £17m or 10% of global turnover.
sentences.article_title: UK plans emergency powers to protect undersea cables

sentences.text: The orders would typically be published, but could be made secret on national security grounds, it added.
sentences.article_title: UK plans emergency powers to protect undersea cables

sentences.text: The proposed powers are not intended to apply to companies operating energy infrastructure,  although the document added that new powers in this area were being considered separately.
sentences.article_title: UK plans emergency powers to protect undersea cables

sentences.text: Ministers said they hoped the new powers would apply across the "full extent" of undersea services, including outside the UK's territorial waters, which extend up to 12 nautical miles from the coast.
sentences.article_title: UK plans emergency powers to protect undersea cables

sentences.text: However, the document concedes this is likely to require co-ordination with other countries, adding that the government was considering how its proposals compare to equivalent regimes internationally.
sentences.article_title: UK plans emergency powers to protect undersea cables

sentences.text: It was also uncertain that existing laws on undersea infrastructure, dating from the Victorian period and designed for telegraphic cables, could be used for breaches of modern fibre-optic cables, the document added.
sentences.article_title: UK plans emergency powers to protect undersea cables

sentences.text: A civil servant accused of fraudulently juggling multiple public sector jobs has told the court he "wasn't thinking straight" when he allegedly misled future bosses about his employment status.
sentences.article_title: 'I wasn't thinking straight' says five jobs civil servant

sentences.text: Kashim Chowdhury said he was "in a panic" when he applied for a job at the Department of Health (DHSC), failing to declare he was already working at the Department for the Environment (Defra).
sentences.article_title: 'I wasn't thinking straight' says five jobs civil servant

sentences.text: The prosecution said he already had three full-time jobs at the time, including roles at the London Borough of Tower Hamlets and East London NHS Trust.
sentences.article_title: 'I wasn't thinking straight' says five jobs civil servant

sentences.text: The 55-year-old, who is from east London, is on trial accused of nine counts of fraud.
sentences.article_title: 'I wasn't thinking straight' says five jobs civil servant

sentences.text: He denies acting dishonestly or intending to make a dishonest gain.
sentences.article_title: 'I wasn't thinking straight' says five jobs civil servant

sentences.text: Chowdhury said he was "in a panic'' because he feared losing his Defra job and was uncertain about his future.
sentences.article_title: 'I wasn't thinking straight' says five jobs civil servant

sentences.text: He told the jury he was "not paying attention, I was not thinking straight',' when filling out the application.
sentences.article_title: 'I wasn't thinking straight' says five jobs civil servant

sentences.text: The prosecution said Chowdhury held five jobs on full-time salaries at the height of the alleged deceit.
sentences.article_title: 'I wasn't thinking straight' says five jobs civil servant

sentences.text: Civil servant faked illness with make-up to juggle five jobs, court hears Civil servant admits he 'made mistakes' juggling five government jobs In the spring of 2023, he was employed by the Defra, the UK Health Security Agency, the Food Standards Agency, the Department for Business and Trade and the Home Office.
sentences.article_title: 'I wasn't thinking straight' says five jobs civil servant

sentences.text: The jury was told that throughout this period he was contracted to work 183 hours a week - more than the number of hours that exist in seven days.
sentences.article_title: 'I wasn't thinking straight' says five jobs civil servant

sentences.text: Each job paid a full-time wage, with Chowdhury paid £11,000 for a single month's work in 2023.
sentences.article_title: 'I wasn't thinking straight' says five jobs civil servant

sentences.text: Prosecutors say Chowdhury "exploited" the work-from-home culture which began during the Covid-19 pandemic to hide his multiple jobs and took sick leave from some employers to manage the workload.
sentences.article_title: 'I wasn't thinking straight' says five jobs civil servant

sentences.text: But Chowdhury told the court he had not wanted the jobs at the DHSC, Department for Business and Trade and the Home Office.
sentences.article_title: 'I wasn't thinking straight' says five jobs civil servant

sentences.text: He told the jury: ''I sent out a flurry of these applications.
sentences.article_title: 'I wasn't thinking straight' says five jobs civil servant

sentences.text: The offers for these jobs came all at once.
sentences.article_title: 'I wasn't thinking straight' says five jobs civil servant

sentences.text: I had discussions with my line managers saying that I did not want these jobs and explained my circumstances.
sentences.article_title: 'I wasn't thinking straight' says five jobs civil servant

sentences.text: These were all short term and probationary and my priority was to look after my mother.'' He added that around May and June 2022, his mother's health "deteriorated".
sentences.article_title: 'I wasn't thinking straight' says five jobs civil servant

sentences.text: He said: "That overwhelmed me at the time.
sentences.article_title: 'I wasn't thinking straight' says five jobs civil servant

sentences.text: It just destroyed me." Chowdhury described the jobs as his "lifeline at the time".
sentences.article_title: 'I wasn't thinking straight' says five jobs civil servant

sentences.text: "They gave me a link to the outside world and were a distraction from what was going on in my personal life, looking after my mum at that time." The prosecution alleges Chowdhury managed to keep his overlapping jobs secret because he worked entirely remotely.
sentences.article_title: 'I wasn't thinking straight' says five jobs civil servant

sentences.text: He told his employers he was the sole carer for his elderly mother and the prosecution alleges he "exploited this opportunity".

sentences.article_title: UK's gaps in Arctic defence leave it open to Russian attacks, committee warns

sentences.text: The Commons Defence Committee said a shortage of Royal Navy warships and submarines was leaving the country's critical infrastructure in the High North, including undersea cables and energy supplies, exposed.
sentences.article_title: UK's gaps in Arctic defence leave it open to Russian attacks, committee warns

sentences.text: In the event of a conflict, the report added that Russia could threaten the UK's population, civilian and military infrastructure and vital supply routes across the Atlantic from the US.
sentences.article_title: UK's gaps in Arctic defence leave it open to Russian attacks, committee warns

sentences.text: The Ministry of Defence (MoD) said it is "clear-eyed about the threat Russia posed" and is investing heavily to protect Britain's undersea cables.
sentences.article_title: UK's gaps in Arctic defence leave it open to Russian attacks, committee warns

sentences.text: Former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer previously warned that Russia could attack Nato by the end of the decade.
sentences.article_title: UK's gaps in Arctic defence leave it open to Russian attacks, committee warns

sentences.text: The High North - which includes the Arctic circle and areas adjacent to it  -  has become central to the UK's defence concerns in recent years.
sentences.article_title: UK's gaps in Arctic defence leave it open to Russian attacks, committee warns

sentences.text: Earlier this year, the MoD said Russian submarine activity in the North Atlantic is now back to the same levels as the Cold War era.
sentences.article_title: UK's gaps in Arctic defence leave it open to Russian attacks, committee warns

sentences.text: In the new report, MPs highlighted a "shockingly low availability" of submarines and said there was a temporary loss in ability to operate them beneath Arctic ice.
sentences.article_title: UK's gaps in Arctic defence leave it open to Russian attacks, committee warns

sentences.text: "Russia can then use the ice to conceal and protect its own submarines while threatening Nato sea lanes, UK critical infrastructure and the UK's nuclear deterrent," it added.
sentences.article_title: UK's gaps in Arctic defence leave it open to Russian attacks, committee warns

sentences.text: Chair of the Defence Committee, Tan Dhesi, said: "This is a demanding, hostile environment, and one that our greatest adversary, Russia, is seeking to dominate for military advantage." The work to address these gaps "cannot start soon enough," he added.
sentences.article_title: UK's gaps in Arctic defence leave it open to Russian attacks, committee warns

sentences.text: In light of uncertainty over US support for Nato, the report said the UK should consider whether the British-led Joint Expeditionary Force (Jef), a UK-led military coalition of northern European nations, should focus more on the High North.
sentences.article_title: UK's gaps in Arctic defence leave it open to Russian attacks, committee warns

sentences.text: An MoD spokesperson said the Jef was already "strengthening Nato's northern flank and increasing our ability to respond rapidly to emerging threats".
sentences.article_title: UK's gaps in Arctic defence leave it open to Russian attacks, committee warns

sentences.text: Conservative shadow minister for war readiness Stuart Anderson said: "If Nato could be at war with Russia as soon as 2030, as the former prime minister warned, that means time is just as important as money.
sentences.article_title: UK's gaps in Arctic defence leave it open to Russian attacks, committee warns

sentences.text: "To deter war we must be ready for it, that means spending money now, not kicking the can down the road until it's too late".

sentences.text: Zara Aleena, a 35-year-old law graduate, was sexually assaulted and murdered by Jordan McSweeney in June 2022 Tougher punishments for offenders who refuse to attend their sentencings will "rebalance the power" in the justice system, the aunt of murder victim Zara Aleena has said.
sentences.article_title: Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family

sentences.text: From next year, prisoners could be blocked from prison visits and confined to their cells for weeks on end if they do not follow orders to go to court.
sentences.article_title: Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family

sentences.text: This builds on an existing law that orders criminals to attend sentencing or face being fined or jailed for another two years.
sentences.article_title: Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family

sentences.text: "A year or two added to a life sentence wouldn't make any difference to an offender.
sentences.article_title: Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family

sentences.text: But taking away these privileges would," Farah Naz said.
sentences.article_title: Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family

sentences.text: Naz said the refusal of the man who murdered her niece to go to his sentencing "left a sense that justice was not quite complete".
sentences.article_title: Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family

sentences.text: Aleena, an aspiring lawyer, was murdered by Jordan McSweeney as she walked home from an east London bar in June 2022.
sentences.article_title: Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family

sentences.text: McSweeney remained in his cell when he was sentenced to life in prison at the Old Bailey later that year.
sentences.article_title: Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family

sentences.text: He was jailed for at least 38 years, which was later reduced to 33 years after he won a Court of Appeal challenge .
sentences.article_title: Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family

sentences.text: Naz said Zara's Aleena's family had hoped that by reading their victim impact statement in front of her murderer, he would see "the consequence of his actions, of what he'd done, the devastation that he had caused".
sentences.article_title: Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family

sentences.text: She added that the new measures would "bring accountability and rebalance the power in the justice system from offender to victim." Offenders who refuse to attend sentencing can already face a fine or up to two years additional imprisonment for contempt of court.
sentences.article_title: Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family

sentences.text: But the Ministry of Justice has acknowledged that longer jail time alone is unlikely to deter those already behind bars.
sentences.article_title: Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family

sentences.text: The new measures mean offenders could be confined to cells for up to three weeks, while social visits could be banned for 27 days and other prison privileges revoked for longer.
sentences.article_title: Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family

sentences.text: Judges will also be able to restrict social visits further to once every four weeks for a period of almost three months.
sentences.article_title: Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family

sentences.text: For criminals aged 18-20, similar restrictions could be handed down, but for shorter periods of time, the Ministry of Justice said.
sentences.article_title: Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family

sentences.text: However, visits from prisoners' children will be exempt from the new sanctions.
sentences.article_title: Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family

sentences.text: "Criminals should not be able to pick and choose when they face justice," Prisons Minister Catherine McKinnell said.
sentences.article_title: Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family

sentences.text: "Refusing to turn up to sentencing is an insult to victims and their families, and offenders must face the consequences," she added.
sentences.article_title: Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family

sentences.text: The families of murdered primary school teacher Sabina Nessa and mother-of-three Jan Mustafa joined Zara Aleena's family in campaigning for changes to the laws.
sentences.article_title: Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family

sentences.text: All of their loved ones' killers did not attend their sentencing hearings.
sentences.article_title: Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family

sentences.text: Thomas Cashman, the gunman who murdered nine-year-old Olivia Pratt-Korbel, and triple crossbow and knife killer Kyle Clifford, also refused to face their punishment in court.
sentences.article_title: Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family

sentences.text: Victims' Commissioner for England and Wales, Claire Waxman, said the announcement followed "tireless efforts of victims' families" not accepting offenders simply "opting out of facing justice".
sentences.article_title: Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family

sentences.text: She said it was "essential" the powers were used "consistently by courts and prisons, so families receive the justice and accountability they deserve".
sentences.article_title: Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family

sentences.article_title: Former Scotland rugby international to go on trial charged with rape

sentences.article_title: Former Scotland rugby international to go on trial charged with rape

sentences.article_title: Former Scotland rugby international to go on trial charged with rape

sentences.text: Among the accusations are that Visser "took intimate images" of her without her consent.
sentences.article_title: Former Scotland rugby international to go on trial charged with rape

sentences.article_title: Former Scotland rugby international to go on trial charged with rape

sentences.text: Prosecutors further claim Visser, from Milton Bridge, Midlothian, isolated the woman from family and friends and was physically violent.
sentences.article_title: Former Scotland rugby international to go on trial charged with rape

sentences.text: A fourth charge says he engaged in a course of abusive behaviour against the woman on various occasions.
sentences.article_title: Former Scotland rugby international to go on trial charged with rape

sentences.text: The accusation lists a total of 26 different claims.
sentences.article_title: Former Scotland rugby international to go on trial charged with rape

sentences.text: A number of them are similar to the threatening behaviour allegation, but also include a string of sexual matters.

sentences.text: One is that he sent an intimate image of the woman to someone else.
sentences.article_title: Former Scotland rugby international to go on trial charged with rape

sentences.text: The indictment goes on to state that the prosecution may present evidence about other matters dating back to 2004, but these are not formal charges at this stage.
sentences.article_title: Former Scotland rugby international to go on trial charged with rape

sentences.text: They feature claims of physical and sexual incidents, threats and controlling behaviour.
sentences.article_title: Former Scotland rugby international to go on trial charged with rape

sentences.text: At the High Court in Glasgow, Ian Duguid, defending, said: "It is a plea of not guilty to the indictment." A trial was set for 12 January 2028 in Edinburgh.

sentences.article_title: Senior detective accused of using AI for decisions

sentences.text: On Thursday, the IOPC said it was alleged the officer used AI to "create policy decisions, assess and manage risk, justify decision-making, and input sensitive operational and personal case data".
sentences.article_title: Senior detective accused of using AI for decisions

sentences.text: The IOPC said the force was concerned the senior detective's use of AI "may not have been in line with guidance and conditions issued by the force".
sentences.article_title: Senior detective accused of using AI for decisions

sentences.text: It said it assessed the detail contained in the referral and decided to carry out an independent investigation.
sentences.article_title: Senior detective accused of using AI for decisions

sentences.article_title: Senior detective accused of using AI for decisions

sentences.article_title: Senior detective accused of using AI for decisions

sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: That's why we're calling for companies to audit these systems, publish the results and have them independently assessed.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: "In our research, we found guidance from the Information Commissioner's Office , external stating that people subject to certain automated decisions have the right to request a human review.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: This compares with 57% of white candidates.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: Vivi says she needs feedback as a jobseeker Business consultant Vivi, who lives in Lewisham, was made redundant earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: She says she has applied for so many jobs that she's given up and started her own company.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: "There's one instance where applications closed on Friday and I got a reply on a Saturday morning basically saying that I should work on my skills and come back in six months.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: But it was so obvious that nobody had assessed my skills." If she had known she could ask for a human to review her application, she might have done things differently.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: "I would definitely go back and ask for a human to look at my application and if it is a 'no', that's fine, but feedback helps me as a jobseeker." Hema was made redundant in June Hema, 49, from Surrey, is an HR and talent professional who has worked internationally across multiple sectors.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: She was made redundant in June and has since tracked more than 100 job applications and recruitment opportunities.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: "If you've got an in-house recruitment team, they know the culture, they can see the type of language that you're using in your CV, in your cover letter, during a phone screen." Of the 425 recruiters CV-Library spoke to, about 90 said they used AI in the CV screening stage.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: Alec Stanwell, director of marketing, believes there is a "perception gap".
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: "Candidates almost universally believe that employers are using AI to screen their CVs, filter them and to screen them as they go through the process and that is happening but nowhere near as much as candidates think it is.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: "That perception gap is a problem because candidates are now writing their CVs, and applications, through the lens of 'an AI bot is going to be reviewing this rather than a human'.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: He adds this is a problem because recruiters are seeing all CVs look the same because "they're all written by AI, or polished by AI".
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: He says this creates a "perfect storm" because AI is then more likely to be used to filter through a large volume of applications.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: "We're going to end up with computers hiring computers, but we're actually in the world of hiring people." In the four years to December 2022, Stanford researchers analysed four million job applications processed by an AI hiring tool , external .
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: Some candidates were rejected from multiple roles more often than would have been expected if they had been assessed by each employer independently.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: The analysis also indicated black and Asian applicants were recommended for jobs at lower rates.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: But the evidence is limited.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: They only looked at one AI hiring tool, and other factors such as education and immigration status could have also played a role.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: The hiring tool assessed did not respond to our requests for comment.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: The people I have interviewed are not talking about any company in particular, but concerns over AI used in recruitment are also playing out in the courts.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: One company, Workday, is facing legal claims , external in the US, alleging that its tools discriminated against job applicants.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: The case is ongoing, but Workday denies the claims and says its tools do not make hiring decisions.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: More generally, it says its tools "support rather than replace human judgement".
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: Barb Hyman's company grades candidates on text-based chat interviews What makes this even more difficult is that AI hiring tools work in different ways, with some not even screening CVs in the first place.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: I spoke to one company that grades candidates on text-based chat interviews.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: Barb Hyman, founder of Sapia AI, said: "We don't know anything about you from a demographic perspective and we don't know whether or not you were hired or not hired for a previous role.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: So I think you've really got to look at the nature of the AI and how it's built.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: "At least in the enterprise space, every company we speak to is very conscious of the EU AI Act, even if they don't see themselves as having to comply with that yet.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: And that requires a level of accountability." She added: "No company ever built a high-performing culture by monitoring its people, and you won't build a fair hiring process by policing candidates either.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: "Start by earning candidates' trust: tell them what you're measuring, how they'll be scored, and give them feedback.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: "We saw a huge uptick in applications, but strangely, they all look the same.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: Our suspicion was candidates all of a sudden were using AI to make the applications themselves." Samways used two different AI tools to help the company understand how much of the content was produced by AI but they "produced such a variety of responses".
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: "We found we couldn't trust them and we had to literally sift through those, applications in a human way in the end.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: "It's just clear that at this point we're not prepared to trust AI for this kind of decision-making." An ICO spokesperson said AI and automation could "make recruitment quicker and more efficient" but "must not come at the expense of people's rights".
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: They said: "Employers should be upfront about when automated decision-making is being used, how it works and how it could affect someone's application.
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: They added: "Existing legal protections, including equality and data protection law, already apply to AI systems, and we will act where additional protections are needed." There seems to be a real fear of the unknown because we are often unsure what happens on the other end once we click "apply".
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: But given it seems AI is here to stay, how can we ensure it's fair?
sentences.article_title: Is an 'AI war' complicating your job search?

sentences.text: Meta has been hit with numerous legal fines this year Meta, the company behind Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp has been hit with its largest fine ever for its business practices.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: A judge in New Mexico on Wednesday ordered the company to pay $25bn (£18.6bn) following a two-week trial earlier this year that found it had spent years lying to the public about how it handled Facebook user data.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: "The lies extend beyond Facebook's data practices as well," the judge said, adding they went to "the heart of Facebook's core business practices".
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: Meta's head lawyer CJ Mahoney said the ruling made it "all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico".
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: The company intends to appeal, a move Mahoney said will be successful.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: The fine is the largest to date against Meta, which has either been fined or agreed to settle several other lawsuits this year, including an $18bn deal with California over child safety.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: New Mexico's lawsuit stemmed from the role of Meta, then still doing business as Facebook, in what became known as the Cambridge Analytica scandal.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: That firm utilised data and information from millions of Facebook users as part of its work in political consulting, including on work related to the 2016 US Presidential election, which saw Donald Trump elected for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: New Mexico had also accused Meta of intentionally misleading the public on how it benefitted from content that included hate speech, and how such rules against it were enforced.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: The jury found the company had intentionally misled the public on those claims, too.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: Meta disputed those accusations.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: "At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech to enforce new rules for what people can say online," Mahoney added.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: Lawyers for New Mexico sued the company over many statements Meta executives had made over the years that user data was never shared with or accessed by third parties without a user's permission, when in reality it had been.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: They claimed that the entire population of the state, roughly two million people, was impacted by Meta's dishonesty regarding the way it controlled user data.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: A jury found that Meta had violated state laws more than 40 million times.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: "For too long, powerful technology companies have operated as though their size and influence put them beyond the reach of the law," New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez said on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: "Today's result makes clear that no corporation is too powerful to be held accountable." The state lawyers sought up to $40bn in fines against Meta.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: Meta had argued anything beyond $3.4bn would be unconstitutional.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: Judge Francis Mathew on Wednesday was direct in his decision to fine Meta an amount roughly equal to its profits each quarter.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: He said Meta's violations of law and misrepresentations to the public about how their Facebook data was used and shared were "willful" and spanned "more than 11 years", stretching from 2010 to 2021.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: Communications between senior executives, including Mark Zuckerberg, were "designed to mislead the public", Judge Mathew wrote in his order.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: While the full amount of the penalty against Meta, based on thousands of violations of state law, was calculated as $219bn, Judge Mathew reduced the penalty to the $25bn fine.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: It follows a $5bn fine levied by the US Federal Trade Commission in 2019 against the company over its data privacy practices.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: Campaigners welcome Meta and YouTube's defeat in landmark social media addiction trial Meta fined $567m in largest child safety ruling against social media giant New Mexico has been one of Meta's most notable adversaries in court.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: The state this year also fined Meta almost $1bn for misleading the public about the safety of its social media platforms for children.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: The judge overseeing that lawsuit ultimately compared Meta to an industrial polluter of the air, with its form of pollution being "the psychological harm and sexual exploitation of children".
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: As large as the fines against Meta are, the company is spending much more on infrastructure as it works to catch up with other tech companies in the artificial intelligence (AI) race.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: Zuckerberg said during a call with financial analysts that Meta's consumer-focused AI tool Muse was already being used by 10 million people.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: "Growing Muse to serve billions of people is both our mission and our strategy," Zuckerberg said.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: To that end, Meta expects to spend at least $135bn this year on mostly AI projects, but could spend up to $145bn.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: The company is spending so much on AI that it reported negative cash flow of more than $2bn - an apparent first for Meta since it listed on the public stock market 14 years ago, according to a BBC review of its past financial documents.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: Cash flow represents the money a company retains after paying for operations and investments.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: So, Meta is now spending more than it brings in, even as it brings in more money than ever.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: Meta's revenue increased 26% for July to September compared to a year ago, hitting $64.5bn.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: Its profits also tripled to $9.8bn.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: Still, the company intends to spend more on AI investments.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: Meta's chief financial officer Susan Li announced a new stock split on the call, in which existing Meta shareholders will receive one new share on non-voting stock.
sentences.article_title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy

sentences.text: Li said the new class of stock was not yet intended for one specific investment, but she alluded to ongoing costs related to AI and said the company could use "more funding flexibility" next year.

sentences.text: "But we continually need to work to overcome those institutional challenges," he added.
