sentences.text: Adrianne says her chronic UTI has impacted her physically and mentally "The impact goes far beyond what people understand - we're talking about pain, urgency, sleepless nights and missing out on your life," Adrianne tells her roughly 8,000 followers in a video on TikTok.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: For nearly five years, Adrianne has lived with a chronic urinary tract infection (UTI) - a condition it took her two years to get a diagnosis for.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: In that time she was wrongly told it was colon cancer, Crohn's disease or even that her partner must have been cheating and had given her a sexually transmitted infection.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: What started as one UTI in 2022 became a debilitating cycle.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: "It has completely stripped me of everything: being able to work properly, my relationships, my friendships, going out, being able to have a normal social life," says Adrianne, who works in digital marketing in London.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: The 29-year-old was eventually diagnosed privately with a chronic UTI - something experts estimate could affect up to 1.7 million women in the UK , external .
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: Men and children are also affected.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: Adrianne is not alone in sharing her story and coping mechanisms on social media to fight the stigma surrounding UTIs.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: A quick search on Tiktok or Instagram shows hundreds of posts of women of all ages talking about the reality of living with recurrent and chronic UTIs.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: "I felt incredibly nervous to put myself out there, but there's now this community of people who can share tips with each other, and understand each other," said Adrianne, saying her posts have had a "really positive response".
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: This video can not be played Like ‘weeing lava’: Living with chronic UTIs A chronic UTI, which has no official medical definition, is an infection with persistent symptoms - even after a standard course of antibiotics.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: It can be caused by bacteria entering the lining of your bladder.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: Even on a good day she struggles to leave the house as she worries about having a flare-up.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: While sending a urine sample to the lab remains the gold standard to diagnose a UTI, "false negatives" can often occur, says Professor Chris Harding, a consultant urologist at Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: Another hurdle is the significant crossover between chronic UTIs and other conditions such as painful bladder syndrome, chronic pelvic pain and endometriosis, says Magda Kujawa, a consultant urologist at Stockport NHS Foundation Trust.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: Adrianne says she felt "dismissed" by doctors while trying to get a diagnosis, and frustrated at repeatedly being given advice around hygiene and hydration, while her symptoms persisted.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: Both experts say health professionals should listen to the patient's story to understand whether symptoms amount to a recurrent or chronic condition or something else entirely.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: Since she started posting online, Adrianne has received messages from other young women who worry they are "dirty" and "not taking care of themselves" or that there is "something wrong with them".
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: "There's definitely still a lot of stigma around why people get them (UTIs), and it all just comes back to education.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: We're not taught about them at school," she adds.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: Laura says not knowing when or how she would get better left her feeling "hopeless" Laura Von Müllen, 26, has also been diagnosed with a chronic UTI and documents her experience on TikTok.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: She says her symptoms "really badly" impacted university, and became particularly difficult to manage when she started working.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: She now works remotely from Kent doing social media management.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: As well as urinary symptoms, Laura says she also experiences heart palpitations and panic attacks.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: "People don't understand, they think it's just a UTI and that it'll clear within three days, but I've still got mine two years later," she says.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: Laura also feels there is still a lot of misconception around UTIs.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: "People have said to me: who have you been sleeping with then?
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: When that's not the case." Adrianne and Laura hope more women sharing their experience will help demystify the condition.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: "I've seen women on social media sitting in baths of disinfectant, all because they were convinced that that they were dirty, and that's why they were getting infections.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: And actually, that just made things ten times worse," Kujawa says.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: While Adrianne and Laura's symptoms are showing improvements, they say it's a "long road to recovery".
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma

sentences.text: A clinical trial has been launched in the UK which scientists hope could cut years from the search for new treatments for Alzheimer's disease.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: It will test multiple drugs simultaneously, starting with two repurposed medicines already used to treat type 2 diabetes and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: The study will examine whether the drugs can lessen symptoms such as memory and thinking problems, and help people maintain their quality of life.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Angela Bucksey, 67, from Cambridgeshire, was diagnosed with Alzheimer's in January and is the first person to begin treatment on the trial, called AD-SMART.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "We have Alzheimer's in the family," she told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "My mother had it and my aunts, so it was a disappointment rather than a shock when I was diagnosed because I knew it would restrict my life.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "But I was determined that it wasn't going to define me." Angela said she felt empowered joining the trial because "at least you are doing something".
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "Instead of just sitting there, you're standing up and saying, I will fight back." Alzheimer's is the most common type of dementia, affecting around 600,000 people in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham, whose father died from Alzheimer's last month, said he knew how it felt to lose a loved one to dementia, and had seen first-hand the devastating impact of the disease on families.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "That's why I'm proud to see this trial being launched in the UK, so that cutting-edge treatments can reach patients here as soon as possible," he said.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: The AD-SMART study is what's known as a multi-arm, multi-stage platform trial where several treatments are tested simultaneously, with the results compared with one group of participants taking a placebo or dummy.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: This means those involved have a higher likelihood of getting an active treatment than in a traditional trial.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: If any drug isn't showing benefit it can be dropped quickly and a new treatment added in its place - the approach has been used successfully in cancer and motor neurone disease.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: The two initial drugs being tested are metformin, used to treat type 2 diabetes, and atomoxetine, for ADHD, which were selected by an international panel of experts.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Both drugs may help reduce brain inflammation, which is a driver of neurodegeneration, said chief investigator Prof Paresh Malhotra, group leader at the UK Dementia Research Institute Centre for Care Research & Technology at Imperial College London.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "For too long, Alzheimer's research has moved at the pace of one drug, one trial, one answer - sometimes taking a decade or more before we know if we've found something that works," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "We are applying advances from cancer and other conditions to accelerate testing of treatments for people with Alzheimer's disease." For the drugs to be successful, the study has to show that they have beneficial effects on thinking and the ability to carry out everyday activities.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "That's what patients and their carers care about," said Prof Malhotra.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Some 1,200 participants with mild to moderate Alzheimer's will be recruited at more than 30 sites across the UK.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Sites in Cambridgeshire, Surrey, London, Southampton and Edinburgh are already open.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Scientists expect to finish evaluating the first drugs in 2030 and, in that time, additional treatments are likely to be added.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: All the participants will have regular health checks including cognitive tests, which will help researchers assess how effective the treatments are.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Angela Bucksey's husband Steve, who is her study partner, told the BBC: "Joining the trial has brought us back from the despair of a diagnosis which everybody recognises is non-recoverable.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: People with a confirmed Alzheimer's diagnosis who would like to take part can register their interest on the AD-SMART website , external .
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: The trial is being led by the UK Dementia Research Institute and Alzheimer's Research UK.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Partners include the National Institute for Health and Care Research, the Medical Research Council and Health Data Research UK, with funding by UK government.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Pope Leo returned to St Peter's Square on Wednesday for his weekly general audience Pope Leo XIV does not need any further treatment following an operation to remove a cancerous growth from his lung, his doctors have said.
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: Test results on tissue removed during surgery confirmed he had had a lung adenocarcinoma, as was initially diagnosed, and that the disease was localised, according to a statement shared by the Vatican.
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: "A subsequent oncological assessment has confirmed that no further treatment is necessary," it added.
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: The 71-year-old was discharged from Rome's Gemelli Hospital over the weekend four days after his operation - stopping to speak to well-wishers as he left the grounds.
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: It comes as he held his first weekly general audience since leaving hospital at St Peter's Square on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: The surgery, which took place on 13 October and lasted for 90 minutes, included the removal of the lower lobe of the Pope's right lung.
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: The pontiff himself had announced during his weekly Sunday prayers that he would be having the procedure - telling those gathered in St Peter's Square that doctors had found a nodule on his lung.
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: He said at the time that it had been caught "at an early stage".
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: Images shared days after his operation, on Friday, showed the Pope celebrating Mass from the hospital wearing green vestments and standing behind a makeshift altar.
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: On the same day, the Vatican said he spoke to Russian President Vladimir Putin over the phone to urge a ceasefire in the blockaded Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky to allow the delivery of food aid, and to call for "dialogue and peace".
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: The pontiff had a similar phone call with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday.
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: Those close to the Pope have also previously said he was keen not to delay a trip to Latin America which is planned for early November.
sentences.article_title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

sentences.text: Farage said he wanted to get more people in the reserves at the event for party supporters as part of Reform's 100 Days to Save Britain tour.
sentences.article_title: Farage vows to scrap tax on armed forces reserves

sentences.text: When questioned by the BBC over a Reform councillor in Plymouth who was investigated and cleared over social media posts, Farage said he was "still part of the party was because everyone believes he's a solid bloke".
sentences.article_title: Farage vows to scrap tax on armed forces reserves

sentences.text: About 100 protesters against Reform gathered outside the Plymouth Arena near the city centre, chanting before, during and after the event.
sentences.article_title: Farage vows to scrap tax on armed forces reserves

sentences.text: Reform leader Nigel Farage greeting supporters at the rally in Plymouth Farage spoke to about 300 Reform members and councillors and opened his speech by paying tribute to Ann Widdecombe, who was killed at her home in Devon .
sentences.article_title: Farage vows to scrap tax on armed forces reserves

sentences.article_title: Farage vows to scrap tax on armed forces reserves

sentences.text: "Let's get more men and women signing up for the reserves." When asked by the BBC about the UK deploying fighter jets to defend Saudi Arabia , Farage said the UK was "not even a player any more".

sentences.text: He said: "Should we help with peacekeeping missions?
sentences.article_title: Farage vows to scrap tax on armed forces reserves

sentences.text: "But what we've got to face up to is the reality that we've lost our ability to be an effective player".

sentences.text: Alice Webb died after becoming unwell following a liquid Brazilian Butt Lift procedure Only properly trained professionals will be allowed to offer high-risk cosmetic procedures like liquid Brazilian butt lifts (BBLs), vampire facials and chemical peels, under long-awaited government plans for England in 2027.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: The government said it wanted to "drive cosmetic cowboys out of the market" and shield people from treatments "that can go badly wrong".
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: Currently, there are no restrictions over who can carry out these 'no scalpel' procedures, which can harm or kill if not performed safely.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: Under the new rules, high-risk procedures for under-18s will also be banned, and rogue providers will face new criminal offences and fixed fines of up to £4,000.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: Sasha Dean from Bedfordshire was left in a coma after receiving a liquid BBL The government began consulting on changes to the cosmetic surgery industry in 2023, but there have been calls for stricter regulations for many years.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: It comes following horror stories of procedures reportedly carried out in Airbnbs, hotel rooms, garden sheds and even public toilets, by "cosmetic cowboys" , external .
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: Women have told the BBC of dangerous complications , pain and permanent scarring after treatment by rogue operators.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: Alice Webb, a mother-of-five from Gloucestershire, died within hours of getting a liquid Brazilian butt lift in 2024.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: That same year, Sasha Dean, from Bedfordshire, was left in a coma after receiving a liquid BBL.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: A BBL is a non-surgical cosmetic procedure in which dermal fillers are injected into the buttocks to alter their size or shape.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: Some of Sasha's treatment took place in a private house and she ended up developing sepsis.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: She told BBC News: "Very quickly it turned into a complete nightmare.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: "I had a heart attack, one of my lungs had collapsed, my kidneys were failing.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: But Mr Keith Allison, from the Royal College of Surgeons of England, said the consultation was "long overdue" and, while welcome, the proposals did not go far enough.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: "Ministers must ensure they do not create a new loophole in patient protection by regulating non-surgical cosmetic procedures more robustly than cosmetic surgery itself.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: "A doctor should not be able to carry out cosmetic surgery simply because they hold a medical license." The government will now ask , external doctors, businesses, regulators, the public and other experts for their say on the draft rules, before plans go through parliament in  spring 2027.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: A licensing scheme for Botox clinics in England to improve safety standards has already been announced.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: In Scotland, laws passed in March mean cosmetic procedures must be performed by, or alongside, certain healthcare professionals in a registered setting.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: Non-surgical procedures are banned for under 18s.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: There are no dedicated regulations around cosmetic procedures in Wales or Northern Ireland.
sentences.article_title: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong

sentences.text: Government failures in care settings created an environment that allowed Covid to spread like wildfire, an official inquiry has said.
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: The sixth report from the Covid inquiry said the care sector appeared to be "something of an afterthought" in the early stages of the pandemic and there was no "protective ring" put around homes as claimed by ministers at the time.
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: There were more than 43,000 recorded deaths involving Covid in care homes between March 2020 and July 2022.
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: The 287-page report also highlighted shortages of PPE for carers and criticised the way hospital patients were discharged into care homes.
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: It said limits on visits caused enormous harm to residents and their loved ones, though it blamed this on care homes themselves.
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: Around 1.5 million adults were either living in care homes or receiving support in their own homes when Covid hit.
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: Action to protect them came too late, causing devastating consequences, the inquiry said.
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: Chair Baroness Hallet said a lack of testing, PPE and pre-pandemic planning combined with policy decisions early on "created an environment in which the virus could spread like wildfire".
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: "At the critical early stages of the pandemic, not enough was done to protect those living and working in care homes," she said.
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: "It shows that the government knew the care sector was extremely vulnerable to a pandemic and yet did nothing.
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: Failing to act until it was too late." Caroline, Abrahams, the charity director at Age UK, said the report was "devastating".
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: "When Covid took off, people using social care and the staff and unpaid carers providing it were left totally exposed." She added it also demonstrated how important the overhaul of social care promised by Andy Burnham when he became prime minister was.
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: "That cannot be allowed to happen again," she added.
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: Nadra Ahmed, co-chair of the National Care Association, which represents care providers in England described the findings as "really upsetting", adding that the social care workforce has "never fully recovered" from the pandemic.
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: She said we need to "start thinking about social care in a more constructive way" and the mantra that "we all had to protect the NHS" appears to have come at the cost of "some care home residents' lives".
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said the government would provide a "full response" to the report's recommendations "in due course".
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: Speaking in the Commons, Cooper said she agreed that social care had been "undervalued and under-recognised" for too long.
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: "My thoughts are with all those who lost loved ones in the pandemic, and especially those who endured the immense distress and harm of visiting restrictions in care homes, which meant they could not be with loved ones even as they died," she added.
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: The sixth report of the Covid inquiry is highly critical of the way the government tried to protect people in care settings in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Around 500,000 people were living in care homes at the start of the pandemic – with another million receiving care in their own homes.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The inquiry said action to protect them came too late, causing devastating consequences.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: There were more than 43,000 recorded deaths involving Covid in care homes between March 2020 and July 2022.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Here are the key findings of the 287-page report.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: At the start of the pandemic, the then-health secretary in England, Matt Hancock, said the UK government had placed "a protective ring" around care homes.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: But the inquiry says this was not the case, listing a catalogue of failings.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: It says the care sector appeared to be "something of an afterthought".
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: A lack of personal protective equipment (PPE) meant staff had to resort to makeshift workarounds, including bin bags, festival waterproof ponchos and painters' overalls.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The report is also critical of the way hospital patients who may be infected with Covid were moved to care homes to make space for others.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The decision was understandable given the need to free up beds for Covid patients.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: But, without sufficient testing, it was important to keep these people separate and isolate them from others in case they were infected.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Official guidance in March 2020 in England, Wales and Northern Ireland did not request this.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: That, the report says, was a significant oversight.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: When the pandemic started, high levels of staff vacancies and turnover in the social care sector meant that the workforce was "fragile and lacking resilience".
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: This undermined the ability of the sector to respond to the pandemic, the inquiry says.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: For example, care homes tend to rely heavily on agency staff who work in a variety of different homes.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: But a desire not to have staff going into multiple homes, to reduce the risk of infection transmission, meant staff shortages got even worse.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Financially, care providers struggled too, as the number of people using services dropped.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: And for a sector that uses zero-hours contracts, there was a lack of financial support to help care staff stay off work if there was concern they might be infected.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The response also suffered because of the fragmented nature of the system, with thousands of different providers and services overseen by councils.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: It meant the sector was more distant from government than the NHS.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The pandemic, the inquiry said, exposed and exacerbated these existing weaknesses.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The report is clear that precautionary steps taken to restrict visiting, as part of infection control, went too far.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: It acknowledges there was little choice to introduce bans on visitors at the start of the pandemic, saying that was rational.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: But as the pandemic progressed, so did the balance between the benefits and harms of restrictions.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Visits are extremely important, allowing loved ones to help residents with everything from personal care to maintaining their mental health.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: By September 2020, evidence suggested visitors posed a "marginal risk" – staff were judged to be the key entry point for infections.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The four UK nations then started to relax their guidance, but many care homes failed to implement this and visiting remained heavily restricted.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: This, says the inquiry, resulted in a significant decline in the health and wellbeing of residents.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: CPR (Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation), including chest compressions, can be life-saving if a person's heart has stopped beating.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: But doctors can sometimes opt not to resuscitate people - as can individuals themselves in advance - for example, if the individual is extremely frail or has a life-limiting illness.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: This should be done on an individual basis and the use of blanket do not resuscitate orders (DNACPR) is considered unlawful.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The inquiry says it heard evidence of GPs imposing blanket DNACPRs on care home residents.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: And it pointed to records showing a sharp increase in orders being put in place – they jumped from 16,800 to 26,500 in the first nine months of the pandemic.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: This concern mirrors an earlier Care Quality Commission investigation which found evidence of unacceptable and inappropriate DNACPRs being put in place.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The impact on staff working in care homes was huge, affecting their mental health and wellbeing, the inquiry said.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Some moved into the care homes where they worked, in an attempt to protect residents from infection.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: One care home owner in Wales described how 39 staff moved in for a fortnight at the start of the pandemic.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Seeing so many residents die placed an enormous strain on workers, who often had to provide end-of-life care to multiple people at the same time.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: One care home, for example, lost half of its residents over the course of three weeks.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Staff told the inquiry of the deep distress they suffered.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: "Staff were sitting on video calls with families, saying their last goodbye to loved ones.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: That was horrendous… staff were crying with the residents, because it was just so emotional for them," one said.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: An AI tool may be able to help doctors judge how ill a patient is using a single photograph of their face, say US researchers.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: Trained on millions of healthy faces, and 35,000 photos of cancer patients, the tool can make estimates on survival by looking closely at features near the eyes, the scientists say.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: While it's a long way from being suitable for use in hospitals, the researchers say their goal is to help doctors recommend the right treatments for their patients.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: The preliminary findings are published in the Lancet Digital Health , external journal.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: The researchers developed two AI tools to estimate biological age and predict cancer survival from a single face photo.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: The face on the left shows features most important to cancer survival outcomes, while the right face shows those key to age.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: Areas shown in yellow had the greatest impact on predictions.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: The 'FaceSurvival' AI tool suggests the area under the eyes and around the bridge of the nose are the most vital parts of the face to assess when estimating how long they might have left to live.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: These metrics applied across many different types of cancers, varying in severity, including ones that had spread to the patient's bones or brain.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: Most of the cancer patients, who were from the US and the Netherlands, were in their 50s or 60s, but some were children, while others were in their 90s.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: Doctors already examine patients and run comprehensive checks and tests to judge how unwell they are, and what their prognosis might be.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: The AI tool, which has a patent application pending, is designed to help doctors doing this work, not replace them.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: Lead researcher Dr Raymond Mak, from Mass General Brigham in Boston, explained: "As the population ages, physicians need better ways to estimate physical reserve and frailty before recommending intensive treatments such as radiation, surgery or systemic therapy.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: "Our goal is to make face photograph-based health assessment more quantitative, consistent and scalable so it can support personalised treatment decisions rather than replace physician judgment." Collagen: Do you drink it?
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: Why doing a mix of exercise could be the key to longer life Can two hours of strength training a week reduce the risk of dying early?
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: Mak and colleagues are also evaluating an AI tool for predicting biological age, or how old someone looks, as opposed to their birthday age.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: The 'FaceAge' tool suggests the skin below the nose and near the mouth - the so-called nasolabial folds and marionette lines - plus the forehead (frown lines), temples (crows' feet) and cheeks are a good indicator of how fast we age.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: Some lifestyle habits can speed that process up, like heavy alcohol use, drug use and smoking.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: Mak says the tool was "surprisingly consistent" across common real-world photos despite variations in pose, lighting, facial expression and make-up.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: "It was also stable across most tested plastic surgery procedures, with only a small shift observed after rhinoplasty [a nose job]," he says.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: But the researchers stress they need much more data and photos of faces, particularly from lots of different ethnic groups, to determine how well the tools work.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: They are still very much under development.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: The research team is inviting the public to take part , external and receive a personalised biological age estimate by uploading their own facial photo the research team.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: Prof Miroslaw Bober, an expert in video processing and machine learning at the University of Surrey in the UK, says any claims that the tool could track ageing or lifestyle changes over time would be "premature".
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: "This is a promising proof of concept, but it is not ready for clinical use," he said.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: "The tool still needs testing against doctors' own judgement and across different hospitals and patient groups." And he warned: "Predicting an outcome is not the same as explaining it." AI can forecast your future health – just like the weather AI designs antibiotics for gonorrhoea and MRSA superbugs

sentences.text: A million young people are being offered a free meningitis B vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It comes after concerns over the UK's largest and fastest growing outbreak that happened in Kent earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Nearly 90,000 doses of the vaccine have already been given, with 135,000 more booked in for the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: So who needs the vaccine, what's in it and where can you get it for free?
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It is common to get some swelling, redness or tenderness where you have the injection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You may also get a mild fever, nausea, headache or muscle aches but these symptoms should disappear after one or two days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: More serious side effects are rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bookings can be made at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Seventeen and 18-year-olds can book via the NHS National Booking Service , external if they are already registered with a GP , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Other students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time can also contact a participating pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You do not need to be registered with a GP surgery to use the walk-in service.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Find a participating pharmacy here , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine, given as two doses and at least 28 days apart, is being offered to 17 and 18-year-olds in sixth form and students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Both doses are needed for the fullest protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Within weeks, in Kent, there were 29 confirmed or suspected cases and two deaths.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: That's why the new, one-off campaign is being launched - to help protect those at greatest risk and hopefully prevent something like this from happening again.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Students in their first year of university have a risk that is about seven times higher than that of young people of a similar age who do not go to university, says NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis infections can be spread through close contact - for example through kissing, sharing vapes and drinks or living in close quarters with a person with the bug.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: UK health officials say the risk to 18-year-olds or those entering university or a residential college for the first time is higher because of increased mixing of social groups and shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: MenB infection can cause serious, life-threatening problems including inflammation of the lining of the brain (meningitis) and blood poisoning (sepsis).
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can lead to life-changing disabilities such as amputations, hearing loss and brain damage, and in some cases can be fatal.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Vaccination can save lives.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: All babies are now offered it.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But it means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young babies are vaccinated because they are more likely to get invasive infections more often than other age groups, and their bodies are less likely to be able to fight them off.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: However, research suggests the MenB vaccine doesn't necessarily prevent transmission of the infection from person to person, doesn't target all the different B bacteria strains and doesn't provide long-term protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But UK vaccine experts now say government should consider routinely offering the vaccine to all teenagers at around age 15 .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It will be up to ministers in each nation to decide whether to do this.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meanwhile, they do want everyone who is eligible to come forward and get the vaccine because it can prevent serious illness.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Around 10,000 people in the Kent region will have already received jabs, as part of the response to the March outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Each nation has its own plans , external , but all are offering the vaccine to most pupils completing Year 13 or S6 in the summer of 2026 - irrespective of their education plans and including people from this age group who are not currently in school.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young people aged 18-25 starting university or moving into residential further education settings for the first time in autumn 2026 are also eligible.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: In Wales, those aged 17-18 will receive a letter invite, while those aged 18-25 who are entering higher education will need to contact their health board later in July.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis can be caused by many different types of viruses or bacteria, which are spread through close contact with a person who has them.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Viral meningitis tends to get better on its own within seven to 10 days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can often be treated at home with plenty of rest, painkillers and anti-sickness medicine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bacterial meningitis needs to be treated in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Outbreaks are thankfully rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Currently, a separate vaccine covering different strains, the MenACWY vaccine, is offered routinely to 14-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down We know some people love a cuppa, even when it's sweltering, and that actually makes scientific sense.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down, says Dr Daly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Research suggests your body sweats more quickly to get rid of the excess heat after a hot drink.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Your body is trying to keep your core temperature steady at about 37 degrees celsius.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So hot tea won't necessarily help you cool down more quickly - the key thing is to stay hydrated no matter the temperature of the liquid.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You don't need to shun your favourite coffee either just because it's hot - although too much caffeine can make the body produce more urine, and leave you dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Franklin was a British chemist and crystallographer, whose X-ray diffraction work helped discover the structure of DNA Rosalind Franklin is the only female scientist named in GCSE and National 5 science exam specifications in the UK, according to new research.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: A Cambridge study found that of the 86 scientists named by UK exam boards, the English chemist, whose work in the 1950s helped reveal the structure of DNA, was the only woman.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Exam specifications set out the skills and knowledge students are expected to have gained by the end of their course and how they will be assessed.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Exam boards said there was "a clear need for greater representation in science qualifications".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Academics from the University of Cambridge, along with institutions in the US and Australia, examined how many women were mentioned in specifications for biology, chemistry, physics, environmental science, geology and astronomy.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Their work, published in the British Educational Research Journal, looked at six exam boards in the UK: At Key Stage 4 and equivalent, including GCSEs and National 5s in Scotland, Franklin was the only woman among the 86 scientists mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: She was also one of three women mentioned at Key Stage 5 and equivalent - including A-levels, AS-levels, National Highers and National Advanced Highers - out of a total of 181 scientists.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Marie Tharp, an American cartographer who created the first map of the floor of the Atlantic ocean in the 1950s, and Inge Lehmann, a Danish seismologist who discovered the existence of the Earth's inner core in the 1930s, both feature in the Cambridge OCR's A-­level Geology.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin, who was named in Cambridge OCR's GCSE Biology and Scottish Highers Biology, produced a famous DNA image known as Photograph 51.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Cambridge scientists Francis Crick and James Watson used the image to work out the following year that DNA has a double-helix structure.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Watson, Crick and Franklin's colleague Maurice Wilkins received the 1962 Nobel Prize for the discovery.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin had died four years earlier.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Academics who wrote the paper found that "several major scientific breakthroughs" in specifications were made by women, but they were not explicitly mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The paper said: "Many of the scientific discoveries and explanations were developed in the 1800s and early 1900s, a period when scientific and mathematical practice was largely, but not solely, dominated by men.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: "Our findings confirm that the UK science specifications reflect this historical imbalance: although women made significant contributions to major scientific breakthroughs, this fact is rarely acknowledged." The academics recommended that Franklin should be included "in all specifications when teaching DNA structure".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: They also said specifications should refer to Marie Curie, who discovered radium and polonium and coined the term radioactivity, and nuclear physicist Lise Meitner, who discovered nuclear fission, among others.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The Department for Education in England said "girls should see the contribution women have made in STEM", adding it was "committed to improving the school curriculum over the coming years, and as part of that will make sure every girl can see where their learning can take them".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The Scottish Government said it was "committed to closing the gender gap in STEM and will carefully consider the findings of this research".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The amount of time children in England spend on screens at school could be harming their "physical and developmental health", a group of more than 150 clinicians has warned.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: GPs, paediatricians and other specialists said in an open letter to Education Secretary Lucy Powell and Health Secretary Yvette Cooper that tablets and laptops are being used without a full understanding of their long-term health impacts, including on eye health.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: The clinicians said they are prescribing glasses, hearing aids and speech therapy to children "for a problem that is unintentionally being made worse in our schools".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: The government said it was consulting on screen time guidance for children aged five to 18 but that technology could be a powerful learning tool if used properly.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: The group of clinicians said nearly one million children are using screens in most lessons, despite studies suggesting a rise in short-sightedness.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: They pointed to an analysis of 276 studies covering 5.4 million participants around the world.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: That analysis, they claimed, found a rise in short-sightedness among children and adolescents from around 24% in 1990 to almost 36% by 2023, warning the condition is associated with an increased risk of a range of eye health problems.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: She told BBC Radio 4's Today programme parents had not been given the chance to "opt out" of the "excessive" use of screens in schools, which risks children "just not thriving" in education.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: She said an "explosion" in short-sightedness "cannot be put down to genetics alone".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: It also warned that children with special educational needs are "disproportionately" directed to screen-based learning.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders, said education technology can provide schools with "very effective learning tools".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: But he said such technology was only part of an "overall learning strategy", which also includes classroom discussion and interaction, and that the school day also has  "plenty of non-screen time such as PE, sport, and break times with classmates".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: "We would welcome the development of practical, evidence-based guidance to support the work of schools in the use of education technology," he added.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: Paul Whiteman, general secretary of the National Association of Head Teachers, said it was "important that a healthy balance is struck", adding that "greater clarity is needed from the government on this".

sentences.article_title: Women welcome annual health checks for condition affecting millions

sentences.text: It is one of the reasons she supports the decision to rename PCOS to polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) earlier this year, alongside a recommendation for annual health checks to improve diagnosis and long-term care.
sentences.article_title: Women welcome annual health checks for condition affecting millions

sentences.article_title: Women welcome annual health checks for condition affecting millions

sentences.text: Not long after beginning university, she started experiencing irregular and painful periods, thinning hair, weight gain and exhaustion.
sentences.article_title: Women welcome annual health checks for condition affecting millions

Neelam described how she was advised to exercise more and lose weight, but her symptoms soon began affecting her studies, causing her to miss lectures and re-sit exams.
sentences.article_title: Women welcome annual health checks for condition affecting millions

sentences.text: She was eventually diagnosed with PCOS, having "never heard" of the condition before.
sentences.article_title: Women welcome annual health checks for condition affecting millions

sentences.article_title: Women welcome annual health checks for condition affecting millions

sentences.article_title: Women welcome annual health checks for condition affecting millions

sentences.text: She later went on to have a daughter, which she said was a "really big surprise".
sentences.article_title: Women welcome annual health checks for condition affecting millions

sentences.text: The charity founder said the renaming of the condition, which supporters said was "more representative" of how it affected the whole body, could help improve understanding, but there was still a "long way to go".

sentences.text: "PCOS itself wasn't even understood.

sentences.article_title: Women welcome annual health checks for condition affecting millions

sentences.text: "If that name change means those conversations come more to light, then I'm all for it." Rochelle Lewis said years of symptoms and appointments left her feeling unheard For many years, Rochelle Lewis, from Wolverhampton, struggled with facial hair growth, painful periods and anxiety.
sentences.article_title: Women welcome annual health checks for condition affecting millions

sentences.text: "I've always struggled with a lot of facial hair growing up, it was something I was really bullied about, so I tried to do absolutely everything I could to try and get rid of it," she explained.
sentences.article_title: Women welcome annual health checks for condition affecting millions

sentences.article_title: Women welcome annual health checks for condition affecting millions

sentences.article_title: Women welcome annual health checks for condition affecting millions
