sentences.text: Ofcom is investigating whether Meta breached its duties under the UK's online safety laws with the launch of its "Instants" feature on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: The tool - allowing users to take and share an instant image with close friends, that disappears once viewed - was launched on Meta's photo-sharing app in May as "a new way to share photos in the moment".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But the regulator said the social media giant had not properly assessed risks posed by the feature prior to launching it - something it is required to do under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA).
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said in a statement that it "takes its regulatory obligations under the Online Safety Act seriously".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," they said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation." Ofcom said its probe would examine whether Meta breached OSA duties by not carrying out "a suitable and sufficient illegal content risk assessment and children's risk assessment before the launch of Instants".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Under the UK's sweeping online safety rules, platforms including Meta must carry out and update risk assessments to comply with a range of duties, including to tackle illegal content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: They must also show how they prevent children permitted to use their services from encountering content deemed harmful for them.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: This spans material relating to pornography, or promoting self-harm or suicide - as "priority primary content" - alongside things like abusive, hateful or bullying content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Our online safety laws are clear – significant changes to platforms must be risk assessed before they're launched," said Ofcom enforcement director George Lusty.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "This is a vital step that tech firms must take to protect their users," he added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Images shared with Instants can be viewed by those who have been selected as "close friends" by a user, or those who they follow and are followed back by.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta says the feature has a range of built-in protections, including for younger users with Teen Accounts, including preventing screenshots, reshares or forwarding of Instants.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But disappearing messages and images have been singled out previously as posing particular risks for child or teen users of some apps .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Safety by design must be built in, not bolted on, and today's investigation shows we'll take action where we have concerns that providers are failing to comply," Lusty added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: All three companies have appeared in court this week, arguing they should not need to provide so much information in response to Ofcom's formal requests.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta has separately also argued Ofcom should not be able to levy fines for breaches based on its global annual revenue.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: It also contends that its messaging and image-sharing apps should not have to face additional requirements under the OSA, such as tackling paid-for fraud ads.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: A woman convinced her former partner she had given birth to two children who most likely did not exist in what a High Court judge described as an "extraordinary" and "elaborate campaign of deceit".
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The man, who has not been named but was referred to as John in the judgement, applied to the Family Court after he was told the woman had sold their two children for a combined £500.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The case heard that the man received messages and photos of the children and paid the woman around £30,000 over the course of two years.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: But in a hearing in February, the woman, who was referred to as Jane, told the judge she had lied about the pregnancies for revenge, claiming the man had abused her.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The court heard the man believed he was the children's' father because in late 2022 his partner told him she was pregnant, sent pictures of an ultrasound image and had become "visibly pregnant" as time went on.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: In May 2023, shortly before the first baby was due, the woman called the police alleging she had been assaulted by the man.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: He was arrested and subsequently held on remand for several months, Mrs Justice Judd said in her ruling which was published on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Following this, the woman sent a message to his stepfather saying the baby had been born as well as sharing baby photos.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: At one stage she is said to have sent voice notes to her former partner's mother in the middle of the night with the sound of a baby crying in the background.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Later, she told the man she was pregnant again and the baby was due in August 2024.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: However, before the due date, the couple split up and did not reconcile.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The woman would go on to tell the man's mother the baby had been born.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The woman admitted to the court she had told him she was pregnant when they were together, and afterwards, but conceded she had told a series of elaborate lies and that there were, in fact, no children.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: She argued she was menopausal at the time and could not have been pregnant and bank statements show she attended a tanning shop on the day she said she had given birth, Mrs Justice Judd said.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: In her judgement, the judge concluded that the "factors that weigh against the children genuinely existing were very strong, stronger than the factors pointing the other way".
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: She said the man was the victim of a "sustained and elaborate campaign of deceit" which also impacted his mother and closest friend.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: "Added to this, the behaviour was cruel, leading a man and his mother to believe they had children and grandchildren respectively.", the Judge said.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The judge added she was unable to conclude the woman's motive for her behaviour but said financial fraud was a "possibility"  and that the "complex mental health problems" she suffered from may have also played a part.

sentences.text: Experts warn children as young as five years old are now being groomed on social media and gaming sites Experts are urging parents to talk to their children amid warnings social media grooming is becoming "quicker" and "easier" than ever before.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Childline said Snapchat, TikTok and Instagram were the top platforms children named in counselling about online sexual abuse last year.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: The companies have been approached for comment.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Avon and Somerset Police's child exploitation prevention officer Andri Nicolau said children as young as five can be targeted through social media, gaming and messaging platforms.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: She urged parents to encourage kids to ask for help without fear of blame or punishment.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: The warning comes after three men were jailed for grooming a 17-year-old girl on Snapchat before raping her.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Research by the NSPCC found sexual communication offences involving children in the South West have more than doubled since the offence was introduced seven years ago, to 756 in 2024/25.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Of those, 300 were recorded by Avon and Somerset Police, 96 by Gloucestershire Constabulary and 61 by Wiltshire Police.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: The charity also said Snapchat was mentioned in 324 counselling sessions about online sexual abuse between April 2025 and March 2026, a 19% increase on the previous year.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: TikTok (234) and Instagram (197) were the next most frequently mentioned platforms.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Chris Sherwood, chief executive of the NSPCC, said: "It's deeply disturbing that hundreds of children have come to us in the past year alone, disclosing experiences of online sexual abuse linked to these popular apps and platforms.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Aqeel used social media, including Snapchat, to arrange to meet young girls.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: He also filmed some of his offences and threatened to share intimate videos and images.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: New data suggests that this particular form of exploitation of children, known as 'sextortion', has also reached record levels.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: The Internet Watch Foundation (IWF) said there has been a sharp rise in the number of young people contacting its confidential Report Remove helpline , external because they fear sexual images of themselves have been shared, or could be shared, online.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Criminals try to extort or blackmail their victims by threatening to publish the images, which have often been taken by the child themselves.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Nicolau said children spending more time online meant they were increasingly vulnerable to grooming, which is "easier" and "quicker" than ever before.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "With online gaming and social media, you have kids from five years old online, some of them have their own phones, so it can be any age," she said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: She works with schools to inform children how to be safe online, but said they are often unaware of the risks, including not viewing people they meet online as strangers and expecting them to be "nasty" from the start.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Nicolau encouraged any child or young person who believes they are being groomed to "find someone they are comfortable with and speak to them".
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: She said the police might not be the first choice, but speaking to somebody they trust is what mattered.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Nicolau urged parents to talk to their children and not take away devices or ban them from platforms, warning this could make them feel they were to blame.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Sit down with your child, tell them it's not their fault, even if they've sent indecent images of themselves," she said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Often, particularly if it's to do with grooming or any kind of sexual or romantic relationship, children can be really scared of being judged and embarrassed to talk," said Bradshaw.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Perpetrators are always adapting ways they can better reach young people, whether that's through gaming or social media," he said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: He said another worrying trend was young people turning to AI rather than adults for advice and support about online harms.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Simmons-Read urged parents to normalise conversations with young people about their online lives.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Ella Bradshaw from the NSPCC said children don't speak out because of fear of judgment Ellen Roome, from Cheltenham, who has been campaigning for improvements to online safety since the death of her son Jools in 2022, said not enough is being done to protect young people on social media.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Children are regularly being fed content that is either violent or grooming material and I think as it stands, there isn't any platform that is fully safe for them," she said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "I do think that the social media ban for children will help, but they need to make sure that it is enforced and social media companies are held to account." Ellen Roome has secured rights for families to get social media data from their children's accounts after they pass away.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Simmons-Read said the social media ban for under 16s , which is due to come into force in 2027, "doesn't go far enough", could be bypassed by criminals and could even discourage young people from speaking up about online grooming.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "We want tech platforms to invest more in detecting exploitation when it's happening on their platforms," he said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: A government spokesperson said it was preparing legislation to make it impossible for children to take, share or view nude images on their devices, which would make the UK the first country to do so.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Alongside this, tech companies must be part of the solution and meet their legal and moral obligations.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Where they fall short, the government will not hesitate to step in," the spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Kerry Smith, chief executive of the IWF, said: "We welcome the commitment to introducing nudity blocking technology on children's devices – but there really is no time to lose." Meta, which owns Instagram and Facebook, said it is working to "fight and prevent grooming in a range of ways".
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said: "This includes restricting contact between adults and teens they're not connected to, and using technology to find and remove known child exploitation imagery.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "We also use behavioural signals to identify accounts showing possible signs of grooming or a sexual interest in children.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Based on the strength of the signals, we either prevent them from finding and following teens or we remove their account completely." Snapchat and TikTok have all been approached by the BBC for comment.

sentences.article_title: NI risks missing 2030 energy goals, says Stormont committee

sentences.article_title: NI risks missing 2030 energy goals, says Stormont committee

sentences.text: During its inquiry, the PAC heard from business and energy sector representatives that uncertainty around future policies and delivery timescales was affecting investment decisions.
sentences.article_title: NI risks missing 2030 energy goals, says Stormont committee

sentences.text: It heard investment could be diverted to Great Britain, Ireland and other European markets where existing factors were seen as more certain.
sentences.article_title: NI risks missing 2030 energy goals, says Stormont committee

sentences.article_title: NI risks missing 2030 energy goals, says Stormont committee

sentences.article_title: NI risks missing 2030 energy goals, says Stormont committee

sentences.text: The Harding's Pits Community Association Group campaigned for three decades to keep it as a wild leisure space Campaigners who have been trying to stop the development of a town's green space have celebrated it being given "village green status" by a council.
sentences.article_title: Activists celebrate as land given protected status

sentences.text: Harding's Pits, seven acres of land beside the River Great Ouse in King's Lynn, had previously been earmarked for a housing development and a supermarket before the Borough Council of King's Lynn and West Norfolk applied to Norfolk County Council for the status.
sentences.article_title: Activists celebrate as land given protected status

sentences.text: The Harding's Pits Community Association Group has campaigned for the past 30 years to keep the area as a leisure space.
sentences.article_title: Activists celebrate as land given protected status

sentences.text: Rick Morrish, 64, the director of the group, said it was a "really great decision... we've struggled to get the village green status for 30 years".
sentences.article_title: Activists celebrate as land given protected status

sentences.text: The application was considered by Norfolk County Council's Planning (Regulatory) Committee on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: Activists celebrate as land given protected status

sentences.text: Morrish told Chris Goreham on BBC Radio Norfolk that "this year's administration got right behind" the cause and it would "give more legal status to protect the site... we're safeguarding it as a public open space".
sentences.article_title: Activists celebrate as land given protected status

sentences.text: Alexandra Kemp and campaigners have been working together to attain protected status for the area Alexandra Kemp, an Independent councillor at the borough council, said she has held nine public events in favour of keeping Harding's Pits as a space for nature.
sentences.article_title: Activists celebrate as land given protected status

sentences.text: "After the long campaign that we fought since 2017 with residents to stop the Borough Council of King's Lynn and West Norfolk putting traffic on Harding's Way, the borough council's support is very important and now protects all of Harding's Pits west of Harding's Way," she said.
sentences.article_title: Activists celebrate as land given protected status

sentences.text: Kemp also campaigned with residents in July against a new car park that the borough council sought to build next to Harding's Pits.
sentences.article_title: Activists celebrate as land given protected status

sentences.text: Visitors can see a whale sculpture in one section of Harding's Pits Morrish said the Harding's Pits Association Group was formed in 2004, adding that the green space was originally a clay pit in the 19th Century, before being used as a landfill site.
sentences.article_title: Activists celebrate as land given protected status

sentences.text: "There is actually rubbish underneath the site," he added.
sentences.article_title: Activists celebrate as land given protected status

sentences.text: Harding's Pits was then turned into a public space in the early 1960s.
sentences.article_title: Activists celebrate as land given protected status

sentences.text: The Harding's Pits is located alongside the River Great Ouse and has cut through routes to King's Lynn town centre The site is currently used for dog walking, accessing King's Lynn town centre, picking fruit such as blackberries and for bird and wildlife spotting, Morrish said.
sentences.article_title: Activists celebrate as land given protected status

sentences.text: He told the BBC that "a hundred species of birds" had been recorded there and it was home to "three or four regular reptile residents, including a lot of lizards" who had enjoyed the warm temperatures this year.
sentences.article_title: Activists celebrate as land given protected status

sentences.text: "Within the town, this is quite a rare asset to have and that's why we think it's so important," he added.
sentences.article_title: Activists celebrate as land given protected status

sentences.text: Cases of antisemitism affecting university students and staff in the UK increased in the last academic year, according to a charity that monitors antisemitic incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The Community Security Trust (CST) said it had recorded 95 "university-related" incidents in the 2025-26 academic year - up from 83 the year before.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said the number had fallen from its peak in the year after Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023 and the war in Gaza began, but remains "substantially higher" than before that point.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Universities UK (UUK) represents more than 140 institutions and said its members needed to "protect Jewish students and staff", adding that the findings were a "serious concern".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Lucy Powell, education secretary in England, said the findings in the CST report were "deeply troubling".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: "We expect universities to take a zero-tolerance approach to antisemitism, and are providing training to help university staff identify and respond to incidents swiftly," she said.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The CST defines an antisemitic incident as "university-related" if it concerns a student, member of staff or academic at a UK university "in their academic or student capacity" - including on campus and online.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: In 2022-23, the last academic year before the 7 October attack, the CST recorded 53 incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: That grew to 272 in 2023-24.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: A report from the charity examining the past two academic years says reported incidents fell in 2024-25 and but grew again in 2025-26.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The most common type of incident recorded by CST over both years was abusive behaviour, including verbal abuse, comments made in person or online and antisemitic graffiti.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Its report said that, for the first time, there were two occurrences of extreme violence in 2024-25.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said there were six reported assaults across both years, eight incidents of damage and desecration to Jewish property - five of which were in student accommodation - and ten threats.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Around two-thirds of reported incidents involved antisemitic language or targeting alongside references to Israel, Gaza, Hamas, the 7 October attack, and the subsequent conflicts in the Middle East.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The war in Gaza was triggered by the Hamas attack on Israel on 7 October 2023 in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others taken hostage.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Israel launched a mass military offensive on Gaza in response which has killed around 74,000 people, according to the Hamas-run health ministry.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: He added that universities had "a duty to ensure that Jewish students and staff can study, work and participate on campus the same as anyone else".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Raphi Leon, president of the Union of Jewish Students, said the report "must be a shot in the arm to boost action to support Jewish students and tackle antisemitism".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Vivienne Stern, chief executive of UUK, said: "The rise in antisemitic incidents in the UK, including on university campuses, is a serious concern.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Natural Resources Wales said it had found the source of the pollution on Friday night A fuel leak in the River Taff which killed fish and sparked a warning for people to shut their windows has now stopped, officials have said.
sentences.article_title: Fuel leak which killed fish in River Taff stopped

sentences.text: On Wednesday, officers from Natural Resources Wales (NRW) said the source of the pollution affecting the Taff in places such as Nantgarw, Treforest and Taffs Well since 16 October was over.
sentences.article_title: Fuel leak which killed fish in River Taff stopped

sentences.text: GE Aerospace previously confirmed fuel got into the river while repair work took place at its site nearby, but NRW said it was working to determine how fuel entered the drainage system and reached the river.
sentences.article_title: Fuel leak which killed fish in River Taff stopped

sentences.text: NRW added it had found fewer than 10 dead fish and impacts to aquatic invertebrates as a result of the leak.
sentences.article_title: Fuel leak which killed fish in River Taff stopped

sentences.text: NRW said the source was identified at 19:30 BST on Friday, after kerosene spread down almost 2.5 miles (4km) of the river.
sentences.article_title: Fuel leak which killed fish in River Taff stopped

sentences.text: It added evidence was being compiled and reviewed as part of the ongoing investigation.
sentences.article_title: Fuel leak which killed fish in River Taff stopped

sentences.text: The environmental body also received reports of pollution affecting the Taff in Glan Y Llyn, Gwaelod-y-garth and Tongwynlais.
sentences.article_title: Fuel leak which killed fish in River Taff stopped

sentences.text: Residents said the area began to smell "like a petrol station" on Friday In an update on Sunday evening, NRW said due to the nature of the incident, identifying how the fuel entered the drainage system was difficult as it involved underground systems.
sentences.article_title: Fuel leak which killed fish in River Taff stopped

sentences.text: Specialist drainage and containment contractors had been sent to the site and were removing the fuel.

sentences.text: It is the hoped the lab will become a hub for upland research A new, purpose-built laboratory will serve as a base for scientists, universities and students to investigate Cumbria's upland landscapes, and how they respond to nature recovery.
sentences.article_title: New lab to become centre for investigating uplands

sentences.text: It is hoped the research facility at RSPB Wild Haweswater, in Penrith, will become a hub for upland science, bringing researchers and conservationists together to carry out fieldwork, share expertise, and develop new collaborations.
sentences.article_title: New lab to become centre for investigating uplands

sentences.text: The lab was funded by the estate of the late ornithologist Denis Summers-Smith.
sentences.article_title: New lab to become centre for investigating uplands

sentences.text: "We want to build on Denis's commitment to field ecology and conservation research, creating a lasting legacy that will benefit both science and nature recovery in Cumbria and beyond," said RSPB's Will Peach.
sentences.article_title: New lab to become centre for investigating uplands

sentences.text: The new lab will support current research through Cumbria Connect, whose work and scientific monitoring spans Wild Haweswater, the Lowther estate and the Lowther Valley.
sentences.article_title: New lab to become centre for investigating uplands

sentences.text: Dr Mo Verhoeven, conservation scientist at Cumbria Connect, explained how the region's landscape is made up of a number of distinctive environments, including peatlands and rainforest, which play a key role in storing carbon and managing water.
sentences.article_title: New lab to become centre for investigating uplands

sentences.text: "Cumbria's uplands are incredibly important for nature recovery," he said.
sentences.article_title: New lab to become centre for investigating uplands

sentences.text: "We hope this laboratory will give researchers, students and conservationists a place to work together and build the evidence needed to guide restoration, both here in Cumbria and in upland landscapes further afield.
sentences.article_title: New lab to become centre for investigating uplands

sentences.text: "It's about making Cumbria a much stronger base for upland science." "Just as importantly, it will help train the next generation of environmental scientists," he said.
sentences.article_title: New lab to become centre for investigating uplands

sentences.text: WhatsApp is introducing new parental controls for teenagers, as tech companies continue to come under pressure to provide more age-appropriate experiences for children.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The social messaging app's new tools will give parents a range of options, such as being told when their child joins or leaves a group.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It will also let them decide on privacy settings for their account.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In a blog post, WhatsApp, clarified parents would not be given the power to see the messages their teen is sending and receiving, which along with calls would stay private and protected by end-to-end encryption.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And it said the controls were optional, which social media analyst Matt Navarra called an "obvious weakness".
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: He said the move was "fairly convenient" for Meta, which owns WhatsApp, because it reduced the company's reliance on age verification by putting some responsibility on parents and teenagers.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "Meta is trying to show regulators we have a child safety system, we have parental controls and we're rolling it out across our platforms," he said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "I think the big unanswered question is whether enough families will actually use it." The minimum age to use WhatsApp is 13 in the UK, although it is higher in some countries.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: According to the firm, parents will be able to adjust or switch off the controls at any time.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The settings will be "straightforward to set up" using a Pin set by a parent, which teens will need if they want to switch off the controls.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Some of the new privacy tools include selecting who can see a child's profile photo and who can add them to groups.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Parents can also choose how their teenager uses Channels, which allows organisations and public figures to send out content.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And they will have the option of choosing between the default 13+ setting for Meta AI, the app's optional built-in AI assistant, or a stricter "Limited Content" option.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "All of these controls are being designed to support open conversations about how to use WhatsApp between parents and teens, while keeping everyone's personal messages private," the company said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The changes come as pressure mounts on tech companies from governments and regulators to change the way they operate in order to better protect children using their platforms.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In June, the government announced it plans to ban under-16s from social media platforms, with the restrictions expected to come into force in March 2027.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It said "highly effective age assurance" measures would be used to check the age of those using social media.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: WhatsApp is currently excluded from the ban because the government considers it a messaging service.

sentences.text: Pupils at the school in Cemaes got the chance to ask question to a NASA astronaut Pupils at a Welsh school were "very excited" when they met virtually with a NASA astronaut.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: Students at Ysgol Cemaes, on Anglesey, were able to put their questions to Frank Rubio on Wednesday, who is set to be part of the crew for the Artemis III mission .
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: Rubio also spent more than a year aboard the International Space Station (ISS) after a fault with the spacecraft that was due to bring him and his fellow astronauts back to Earth.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: During the virtual session, pupils asked him about his experiences of living and working in space, as well as the challenges and excitement of space travel.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: Astronaut Frank Rubio was stranded on the ISS for 371 days This is not the first time pupils at the primary school have had the chance to speak with astronauts.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: Earlier this year, they took part in a project to design a badge that was sent into space, later seeing it float in zero gravity aboard the ISS.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: The opportunity was made possible by former pupil Dr Melanie Coathup - a scientist who works closely with astronauts and has helped inspire the school's growing links with the space industry.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: Guto Rhys, acting headteacher, said the students were "extremely excited" ahead of the meeting, and had "been looking at videos of life on the ISS and life in space".
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: The school's headteacher says the pupils were very excited to talk to an astronaut The pupils had prepared many questions to ask Rubio.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: Harry, 9 and his friend Sofia, 8, were among those listening to the astronaut talk about his experiences.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: Harry said: "The most interesting thing I've done today is learning about NASA and Frank Rubio." The pupils had been busy preparing in the classroom ahead of the meeting, according to Sofia.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: She said: "In the school today, we've been learning about Frank Rubio.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: We learned that if you're sick in space, there are medical kits to help.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: "We've been watching some videos about how to brush your teeth and sleep in space." Harry and Sofia were both delighted to meet Frank Rubio Lola, 9, was also in the hall for the talk on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: She was delighted to see Rubio holding a badge that one of the pupils at the school had designed.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: "We've been learning about Frank Rubio and that he was supposed to stay in space for six months, but he ended up staying there for a year," she said.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: "The most interesting thing that I learned today was that there is a space station up in space," she said.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Spacecraft heading to Mars' moon Phobos lifts off from Japan A spacecraft has launched from Japan headed for Mars' moon Phobos, where it will attempt to grab some moondust and bring it back to Earth.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: If it is successful, this will become the first time a sample has been returned from Mars or its moons to be analysed in laboratories here on Earth.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: The spacecraft is scheduled to arrive at Phobos in August 2027.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: It is hoped that the Mars Moons Exploration (MMX) mission, which is led by the Japanese Space Agency, will solve the mystery of how Mars's moons formed.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Prof Sara Russell, from the Natural History Museum, who is the MMX mission's deputy for sample analysis, said: "There hasn't yet been a successful mission to go to Phobos and bring a bit back to Earth.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "I think this is an incredibly ambitious and fun mission," she said.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: There are only three moons in the inner Solar System: our own Moon, and two around Mars, which are called Phobos and Deimos.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Both of these are tiny - Phobos is about 20km (12 miles) across and Deimos is about 10km (six miles) across.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: They are also irregularly shaped, looking a bit like space potatoes.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: The MMX spacecraft will study Deimos as it arrives in the Mars neighbourhood, and then will focus on Phobos.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: It plans to set down a small rover to explore the terrain, though this will be no easy feat.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Sara Russell says no one has ever landed a rover on such a small moon.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "The moon itself doesn't have very much of its own gravity," she explained.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "But it's next to an enormous planet that's got a much higher gravity,  and that makes it much harder to get a rover onto the surface." Mars got its moons about 4.5bn years ago - but no one knows how they formed The rover will scout out a landing site so that the MMX spacecraft itself can later touch down on Phobos.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Once on the surface, it will deploy a robotic arm and two samplers to grab some moon dust.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: This material will be packed into a small capsule that will return to Earth in 2031, landing in the Woomera desert of South Australia.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: The amount of material that will come back is tiny - just 10g.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "It's a very small [amount] actually," said Dr Chrysa Avdellidou, from Leicester University, who is working with the Japanese mission.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "However we can do several studies even on individual grains… You don't need to have kilos back from a surface in order to do science.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: So it's worth every gram," she said.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: The spacecraft will collect 10g of moon dust from the surface of Phobos Scientists believe the sample will finally shed light on the puzzle of where Mars's moons came from.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: There are two competing ideas.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Either a space rock smashed into Mars early in its history, and Phobos and Deimos were created from the debris.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Or the moons are two wandering asteroids from the outer Solar System, which were grabbed by the Red Planet's gravity.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "When we get the sample back, we'll be able to look in detail at its chemistry and its mineral composition - and the two hypotheses will produce very distinct results," said Sara Russell.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "It should be pretty much immediately obvious.. whether it's the product of this dramatic impact or whether it's a captured asteroid.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: So we'll find that out really quickly." The team is also hoping there might be an extra bonus coming back to their labs.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "One of the really exciting things is that Phobos is so close to the Mars surface that whenever there's an impact into the Mars surface, little grains might actually become implanted into Phobos itself," said Russell.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "And that means that the sample we get back may actually contain grains of Mars as well.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: So it can give us really direct information about the composition and history of Mars." Martian meteorites are rare - this one is on display at the Natural History Museum Bringing material from Mars back to Earth has long been an ambition of space scientists.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: The Nasa Perseverance rover, which has been exploring Mars since 2021, has been carefully collecting samples on Mars and storing them in canisters.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: But a second Nasa/ESA mission, called Mars Sample Return, that would have picked up and returned these canisters, has been effectively cancelled, after its funding was halted by the US Congress.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: China is planning its own sampling mission to Mars, set to launch in 2028.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: It will attempt to return Martian material to Earth in 2031.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: We do already have some fragments of the Red Planet here on Earth in the form of Martian meteorites.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: These are pieces of Mars that were blasted off the surface by asteroid strikes, and ended up being hurled towards the Earth.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Martian meteorites are extremely rare, but like all space rocks that fall to our planet, they become contaminated as soon as they get here, mixing with the air, dust, soil and water.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Scientists are so desperate to get their gloved hands on a direct sample from Mars and its moons because it would be pristine.

sentences.article_title: Astronaut surprise video leaves pupils starstruck

sentences.article_title: Astronaut surprise video leaves pupils starstruck

sentences.text: "We didn't expect to get what we got really," she said.
sentences.article_title: Astronaut surprise video leaves pupils starstruck

sentences.article_title: Astronaut surprise video leaves pupils starstruck

sentences.article_title: Astronaut surprise video leaves pupils starstruck

sentences.article_title: Astronaut surprise video leaves pupils starstruck

sentences.text: The UK government says it is working to identify any potential exposure in its online services, after critical cyber-security flaws were identified in the PHP programming language that underpins a significant number of the world's websites.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: Governments and some of the world's biggest companies are rushing to protect systems that use PHP before hackers can exploit the flaws.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The flaws were first discovered by AI, after which governments urged anyone who uses PHP to address them.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: A UK government spokesperson urged "all organisations, private and public, large and small" to follow guidance to protect their systems.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), as well as its counterparts in the EU and Australia, earlier urged those who use PHP to apply the fixes.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: "Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated," the NCSC said in a statement. , external Amazon said its threat intelligence system identified it was targeted on Saturday.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: It added there were further "exploitation attempts" once the embargo on the flaw warning was lifted.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The company said it "automatically detected and restricted malicious scanning attempts targeting this vulnerability." PHP powers a vast number of platforms, including online shops, Wikipedia and WordPress – the content management system behind many websites like blogs.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: When you visit a website like Wikipedia, PHP is the code that collects information you need and presents it in a way you can read on the web.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: Surrey Centre for Cyber Security Prof Alan Woodward said the flaw affects some 30 million websites.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: As well as the scale of the flaw, Woodward said the nature of it means "an attacker can get their own code on to the webserver and run it and basically do whatever they like." "They can steal data , they can go to other parts of your network.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: All sort of things like that - even plant a backdoor to get in later on, so it's pretty serious," Woodward told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: This video can not be played Why have websites around the world been taken down?
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: BBC explains Cyber security researcher Ryan Austin, who has been researching PHP security for the last 20 years, said he discovered the flaw in the programming language.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: He told the Today programme it was "the most serious vulnerability I've ever found" which "started with a hunch that I would not have been able to scratch without AI".
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: Austin described PHP as "one of the first web languages that powered the early internet".
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: "It's in a lot of places that you wouldn't expect to be that are basically very core to how the internet runs in a lot of ways.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: It's like all the old things that are in a house that you know keeps it [running] but you don't really think about," the PHP researcher said.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: But Austin said this incident is not necessarily bad news because organisations would now "run and patch PHP immediately" if they haven't already.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: Listen to BBC Radio 4 Today programme on BBC Sounds Amazon announced on Wednesday that it had identified a "PHP2Shell exploitation attempt" that occurred on 17 October.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: In the attack, an anonymous internet address attempted to target weaknesses in one of Amazon's decoy or "honeypot" systems, the company's security chief CJ Moses said.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The use of an anonymous IP address suggests that the activity was conducted by a "threat actor", he said.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: While the PHP Foundation intended to release its discovery later this month along with a complete fix for the problem, usually referred to by software developers as a "patch", details of the flaw were leaked on social media on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: In subsequent attacks on Amazon that occurred on 21 October, "the actual payloads and choices in anonymisation infrastructure varied, suggesting these were multiple actors," Moses said.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The attacks occurred after the leak, but before the embargo was lifted on the PHP warning.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The use of AI means that "more actors can act within hours or even minutes once technical details of a vulnerability are disclosed", Moses added.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The PHP incident has "demonstrated how quickly AI is changing our cybersecurity landscape", Australian Council on AI Strategy CEO Anna-Maria Arabia told the BBC, as "what used to take months, to expose a vulnerability, is now taking days".
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: She warned that threats would only become more commonplace as AI technology rapidly improves.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: It is "not going backwards, in other words", she said.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The PHP flaws went undetected for at least a decade.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: Cyber-security firm Wiz has estimated that "roughly 70%" of the internet is affected, though the BBC is unable to independently verify that figure.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The websites for several BBC programmes including Doctor Who and The Traitors are currently inaccessible.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: They have not confirmed a link to PHP - BBC News has approached them for comment.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) said it had followed guidance to take its website offline, "in view of the critical security issues affecting PHP".
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: Edinburgh and Oxford council websites also went offline on Wednesday, but are now accessible.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: What is PHP and why did it spark a global cyber security scramble?
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The Dutch cybersecurity agency went offline as a precaution, and Finland's government shut down its public web services.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: Wikipedia also took down parts of its website.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: This was in line with advice issued by governments, including the US, to take websites down if the flaws could not immediately be fixed.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The US National Security Agency said that the vulnerabilities identified "often provide a direct path to the server's file system or database".
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: It could allow attackers to "steal sensitive data, disrupt services, or move deeper into a network.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: These vulnerabilities are flaws in PHP itself, not in the hosted application or its configuration," the NSA said in a later update.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: OpenAI called the discovery, "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory".
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman has won a dismissal of a lawsuit brought against him by his sister that claimed he had sexually abused her more than two decades ago.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wins dismissal of sister's lawsuit

sentences.text: A US district judge dismissed the case after Ann Altman had refused to attend an independent medical examination, adding she was warned a failure to do so would result in the case being thrown out.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wins dismissal of sister's lawsuit

sentences.text: Ann Altman had claimed the OpenAI founder had regularly sexually abused her between 1997 and 2006.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wins dismissal of sister's lawsuit

sentences.text: Sam Altman has denied those accusations.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wins dismissal of sister's lawsuit

sentences.text: The Altman family has said Ann Altman has mental health challenges and they have supported her financially, adding the claims were made as she continued to demand more funds.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wins dismissal of sister's lawsuit

sentences.text: District Judge Zachary Bluestone said that despite multiple accommodations and multiple opportunities to do so, Ann Altman did not appear for an independent medical exam on three separate occasions, and "failed to meaningfully prosecute her case".
sentences.article_title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wins dismissal of sister's lawsuit

sentences.text: "We broke up and I no longer see my child.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: Firefighters have been battling the stubborn blaze for weeks now When the sun hits the smog enveloping Indonesian Borneo, it turns everything the colour of rust.

sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: There are few better words than "apocalyptic" to describe the way this looks.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: "Sometimes at night my baby's chest makes a rattling sound," she says.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: "She was hospitalised for bronchopneumonia when she was just a month and a half old, and every single night I worry: Will my child cough tomorrow?
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: "Those thoughts haunt me every night." Nastiti lives in Palangkaraya, at the frontline of a months-long environmental catastrophe that has blanketed large parts of Southeast Asia in a toxic haze.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: Wildfires have torched some 1.9 million hectares across Indonesia since the start of the year, according to open-access satellite platform Nusantara Atlas – an area roughly the size of the US state of New Jersey, or the entire landmass of Fiji.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: One million hectares are thought to have burned in September alone.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: But the toxic fallout is larger still.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: Swathes of smouldering forest, swamp and peatlands have turned the air thick with microparticles and carbon monoxide, creating a noxious cloud that has swaddled Indonesia and drifted as far as Singapore, Malaysia and the Philippines.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: As of mid-October, Indonesia's Health Ministry had recorded more than 277,000 cases of people suffering from chronic coughs and acute respiratory infections.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: More than 62,000 of those were infants and toddlers under the age of five.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: "The forest fires have had a huge impact, especially on everyone's health," says 22-year-old Natari Victoria, who was admitted to a health centre in Palangkarya after suffering from a cough for more than a week.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: "I have young cousins, including babies, who are coughing too.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: It's really taking a toll on them." Dianyra Eka Nastiti is worried about how her children will recover Haze and smoke from peat fires contain a complex mixture of pollutants that pose serious health risks to the human body.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: Among these are tiny microparticles which can penetrate deep into the lungs and, in some cases, enter the bloodstream, causing inflammation, chronic lung diseases and increased risk of premature death.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: Another concern is the toxic greenhouse gases that are being unleashed into the air.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: "Here in Central Kalimantan, especially in Palangkaraya, the sky has turned yellow and hazy," says Riduan, head of the Palangkaraya Health Office.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: "So what are the residents actually breathing in?
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: And what happens as a result?
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: The body – specifically the brain – doesn't get enough oxygen." Children, older adults and pregnant women are particularly vulnerable to the dangers of haze, especially during prolonged periods of exposure, when the health impacts can accumulate.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: And when the haze grows heavy, she is quick to force them inside.

sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: That's still well down on the recent peak rate of 9% under Biden in 2022, but higher than the 3% rate that Donald Trump inherited in January 2025.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: Economists estimate , external US inflation would have been lower without the new tariffs imposed by Trump since he returned to office.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: While the impact of the Iran war on global energy prices, with the significant disruption to oil and fuel supplies from the Middle East, has also helped push up US domestic inflation.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The price of a gallon of diesel in the US , external - a fuel used not only by drivers but also widely in agriculture and industry - hit a record high of $6.52 in September.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The price of some grocery staples , external like beef and coffee have risen since Trump returned to office, though the price of eggs has fallen.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: And some US retailers have warned , external that rising energy prices caused by the Iran war will make producing food more expensive and raise prices at the till.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: Average US household incomes are still rising under Trump.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The median income - after adjusting for inflation - rose 2.6% in 2025 to $87,460, the highest on record , external .
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The richest 1%, by contrast, are estimated to be an average of $12,560 better off than they woud have been, primarily because of Trump's tax cuts.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: ITEP's estimates about the impact of tariffs on American households of different income levels are broadly similar to those of the Tax Foundation think tank , external .
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: Trump predicted his tariffs would result in America being "flooded with jobs" , external as manufacturing firms set up new factories on US soil to avoid their products being taxed at the border.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: Since he returned to the White House, an average of 34,000 jobs have been added to the economy each month. ​​But that is significantly down on the 122,000 jobs added each month in the final year of Biden's presidency , external .
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: And the number of Americans employed in manufacturing , external - 12.6 million in September 2026 - is slightly lower than it was when Trump's second term began.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: However, the US unemployment rate remains relatively low , external at 4.2%, which is broadly where it was when Trump returned to the White House.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: Part of the reason for this is Trump's immigration crackdown and deportation programme, which has reduced the size of the available US workforce , external and means a lower number of jobs need to be created each month to stop unemployment rising.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: US government borrowing has increased in Trump's second term, partly driven up by his significant tax cuts .
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The federal government deficit - the gap between its revenues from taxes and its spending - was $2 trillion in the year to September 2026 , external .
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: That's equivalent to around 6% , external of US GDP.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: And the US deficit is projected to rise to above 8% of GDP by 2030 , external .
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: That high rate of government borrowing is itself helping to boost US GDP growth.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The IMF has warned that excessive US government borrowing , external , which it uses to bridge the deficit, and its rapidly rising national debt are raising the risk of a future financial crisis in America.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: This would have a deeply damaging impact on most American households.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The growing deficit is also one of the reasons the US government gets charged more to borrow money in financial markets.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The 10-year US government bond yield has risen sharply since Trump returned to office in January 2025 and is now above 5%, the highest rate since the global financial crisis in 2007.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: That increase in the market cost of US government borrowing also puts upward pressure on the interest rates on mortgages available to American households.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The interest rate on a new 30-year US mortgage has risen to 7.4% , external per year, up from 6.9% when Trump returned to the White House.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: That's added to problems in the US housing market, making homes less affordable for new buyers.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: It has left many existing owners reluctant to move because doing so would mean giving up their cheaper mortgages, which they took out at lower rates , external and cannot take with them to a new property.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?
